item.title: Divots, howlers and bad decisions - dissecting Man Utd's draw in Lisbon
item.description: Manchester United were held to a draw in a chaotic and controversial Champions League encounter with Sporting in Lisbon with Mauricio Pochettino denied a first win as United head coach despite his side turning around a first-half deficit. They were behind at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded from a penalty he gave away – having saved another just minutes before. United then had a goal disallowed before scoring a penalty of their own through Bruno Fernandes, who then put them in front with the help of a large divot on the pitch. There was more drama as Lammens dropped the ball for Sporting's equaliser before Pochettino's side had what they thought was a winner ruled out. Polish referee Szymon Marciniak was at the centre of much of the drama with midfielder Youri Tielemans sent off in stoppage time. BBC Sport breaks down each incident after a crazy night. Lammens saves penalty (30 mins) Lammens saved a poor penalty from Sporting's Luis Suarez, given after Lisandro Martinez left a leg out which caught Geny Catamo. The Belgium keeper got down to hold on to Suarez's low effort which looked set to be a huge boost for the underperforming United number one. Suarez scored the second from the spot [Getty Images] Sporting score second penalty (31 mins) Lammens went from hero to zero in the space of 76 seconds as he rushed out of his goal and took out Maxi Araujo in the United box. Noussair Mazraoui was caught out by a ball over the top but it was reckless from Lammens and this time Suarez buried the spot-kick. Former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "There is no way Senne Lammens can get there. Just stay in the goal." United 'goal' ruled out (40 mins) Amad Diallo thought he had equalised for United before half-time when he headed in after his first attempted was turned on to the cross bar. However, referee Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul against Youri Tielemans. Replays showed Tielemans won the ball and pulled out of the challenge after he played the ball through to Amad. BBC Sport's Dale Johnson: "Marciniak believed that Goncalo Inacio had been fouled by Youri Tielemens on the edge of the area as the Manchester United midfielder played a pass through. "Rather than immediately blow his whistle, Marciniak held off to let the move play out. "But when Diallo hit the bar with his first effort, Marciniak blew his whistle. "Play was dead at that point, so when Diallo then nodded the rebound over the line the VAR was locked out. "However, the chances that the VAR would have intervened were very slim. "Tielemens, who was booked, caught Inacio's foot under his body sliding to make the pass, causing the Sporting defender's ankle to buckle." Former Manchester United midfielder Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "It's an absolute disgrace. I don't know how the referee is seeing that Tielemans has kicked the player. item.content:encoded: Manchester United were held to a draw in a chaotic and controversial Champions League encounter with Sporting in Lisbon with Mauricio Pochettino denied a first win as United head coach despite his side turning around a first-half deficit. They were behind at the break after goalkeeper Senne Lammens conceded from a penalty he gave away – having saved another just minutes before. United then had a goal disallowed before scoring a penalty of their own through Bruno Fernandes, who then put them in front with the help of a large divot on the pitch. There was more drama as Lammens dropped the ball for Sporting's equaliser before Pochettino's side had what they thought was a winner ruled out. Polish referee Szymon Marciniak was at the centre of much of the drama with midfielder Youri Tielemans sent off in stoppage time. BBC Sport breaks down each incident after a crazy night. Lammens saves penalty (30 mins) Lammens saved a poor penalty from Sporting's Luis Suarez, given after Lisandro Martinez left a leg out which caught Geny Catamo. The Belgium keeper got down to hold on to Suarez's low effort which looked set to be a huge boost for the underperforming United number one. Suarez scored the second from the spot [Getty Images] Sporting score second penalty (31 mins) Lammens went from hero to zero in the space of 76 seconds as he rushed out of his goal and took out Maxi Araujo in the United box. Noussair Mazraoui was caught out by a ball over the top but it was reckless from Lammens and this time Suarez buried the spot-kick. Former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "There is no way Senne Lammens can get there. Just stay in the goal." United 'goal' ruled out (40 mins) Amad Diallo thought he had equalised for United before half-time when he headed in after his first attempted was turned on to the cross bar. However, referee Marciniak blew his whistle for a foul against Youri Tielemans. Replays showed Tielemans won the ball and pulled out of the challenge after he played the ball through to Amad. BBC Sport's Dale Johnson: "Marciniak believed that Goncalo Inacio had been fouled by Youri Tielemens on the edge of the area as the Manchester United midfielder played a pass through. "Rather than immediately blow his whistle, Marciniak held off to let the move play out. "But when Diallo hit the bar with his first effort, Marciniak blew his whistle. "Play was dead at that point, so when Diallo then nodded the rebound over the line the VAR was locked out. "However, the chances that the VAR would have intervened were very slim. "Tielemens, who was booked, caught Inacio's foot under his body sliding to make the pass, causing the Sporting defender's ankle to buckle." Former Manchester United midfielder Ashley Young said on BBC Radio 5 Live: "It's an absolute disgrace. I don't know how the referee is seeing that Tielemans has kicked the player. "On first viewing, I thought his foot must have hit him on the follow through but when you look at it again, Tielemans actually tries to take his foot away. "He doesn't touch him because he knows the midfielder is coming towards him. "It is one of the worst decisions I've seen with a referee giving that decision." Fernandes scores penalty (47 mins) United got back on level terms after a foul on Martinez in the Sporting area by Eduardo Quaresma led to a penalty. Bruno Fernandes converted. Former Manchester City defender Nedum Onuoha told BBC Sport: "Martinez wins that penalty, but it is a penalty." Divot assist for Fernandes (49 mins) United took the lead with two quick-fire goals but in bizarre circumstances as Fernandes' speculative strike looked like it would be easily collected by Kaique Pereira only to hit a divot on the pitch and fly up past the Sporting goalkeeper. Former Rangers striker Ally McCoist on TNT Sports: "I think it hits a divot and it jumps over the goalkeeper! That is absolutely incredible." Hargreaves added on TNT Sports: "Unbelievable. It is like a golf divot. There are holes in this pitch absolutely everywhere. "Bruno Fernandes created a divot, does he get an assist for that?" Lammens howler gifts equaliser (80 mins) Lammens made another error, spilling a high ball under little pressure from Suarez. The Sporting striker then reacted quickly to find the target with an overhead kick to make it 2-2, the goal given after a quick VAR check. McCoist: "I am baffled because the forward does what you expect him to do. "The goalkeeper, instead of concentrating on the ball, he thinks about the player." Referee Marciniak was centre of attention [Getty Images] United winner chalked off (82 mins) United thought they had taken the lead as Sporting keeper Kaique appeared to push the ball into his own net from a Fernandes corner. However, after a VAR intervention, the 'goal' was then disallowed for a foul on the goalkeeper by Patrick Dorgu. Onuoha: "First that was an absolutely disastrous goal for United to concede for the equaliser. it comes from a nothing ball into the box, too. "For the United goal that has just been ruled out, the keeper has pushed it into his own net before Dorgu has touched him." Young added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. "If a referee is on the pitch and being sent to the screen, if he's given the goal then stand by your decision." Tielemans was sent off for a second bookable offence [Getty Images] Tielemans sent off (90+3 mins) Midfielder Tielemans was then sent off for a late challenge on Sergi Altimira. The Belgium international's second yellow compounds the controversial one he received in the first half. United have now received five red cards in all competitions this season - two more than any other Premier League side. Young added: "The referee's performance was just simply 'wow'. "The decisions that he gave. Youri Tielemans getting booked to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking and it should have been an equalising goal. "His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace." item.title: Badgers make multiple changes to starting lineup after slow start to season
item.description: Austin Rapp #22 of the Wisconsin Badgers dribbles the basketball while being defended by Jordan Rogers #3 of the Denver Pioneers at the Kohl Center in Madison, Wisconsin, on November 2, 2026. (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers have not enjoyed the best start to the 2026-27 season, losing both of their games at the Baha Mar Championship last weekend. It has been an underwhelming start for several players for Wisconsin, as they try to figure out their new-look roster that features several transfers and a key freshman contributor. So far, head coach Greg Gard has been tinkering with his rotation minutes, trying to figure out his best lineups, as Wisconsin has seen ups and downs in nearly every game so far this season. To make matters worse, Jack Janicki, a key cog for the Badgers bench, is now out for the season with a foot injury. Well, Gard’s experimenting is now transitioning to the starting lineup, as the Badgers are going with a new starting five against the Northeastern Huskies on Wednesday night. Wisconsin is replacing transfer Eian Elmer with freshman Jackson Ball in the backcourt alongside Owen Foxwell and Braeden Carrington. Additionally, Austin Rapp will make his first start of the year, replacing Victory Onuetu in the starting lineup. Elmer was the Badgers’ prized transfer addition from Miami of Ohio in the offseason. He seemed to be a quality fit on paper with his shooting ability and athleticism on the wing. Elmer had also been testing the NBA Draft waters, receiving some interest there before withdrawing and entering the transfer portal. However, the senior has struggled as of late, and his minutes have diminished as a result. After scoring 18, 11, and 12 points in Wisconsin’s first three games, Elmer was scoreless against Seton Hall last week and had just two points against Murray State. A key issue has been the lack of aggressiveness. Elmer had just one shot attempt against Seton Hall and was 1 for 5 against Murray State. Even in the earlier games, there seemed to be some passiveness from the senior in attacking lanes and initiating offense, and his minutes dwindled as a result. Looking for a spark, Wisconsin is going to the freshman Jackson Ball instead. While he’s seen his ups and downs, Ball has looked to be aggressive when in the game, and had 12 points in his most extended action against Murray State last Friday. In the frontcourt, Austin Rapp is back in the starting lineup for the first time, replacing a struggling Victory Onuetu, who has not looked great to start the year. Rapp had been recovering from an offseason procedure, and the move seemed inevitable, although Wisconsin had also seemed to have an interest in playing Nolan Winter with a center. We’ll see how the Badgers rotation changes as a result, but Wisconsin is going with a new starting five against Northeastern here on Wednesday.

item.title: 'I've never seen anything like this': Mike McCarthy walked past reporters listening to Aaron Rodgers rip him on 'The Pat McAfee Show'
item.description: Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers spent Wednesday afternoon savaging Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ best attempt to keep the spectacle out of their own building amounted to changing the channel. According to Tim Benz , who has covered the team for 25 years, about 30 media members waiting for the post-practice locker room session had gathered around a television in the facility’s lobby, transfixed by Rodgers’ ESPN appearance, until a team staffer came through and flipped the channel to How I Met Your Mother . To corroborate this, we were all waiting to go into the locker room after practice. We were watching Rodgers on @PatMcAfeeShow on a TV in the lobby. A team staffer came through and changed the channel to “How I Met Your Mother.” So we all just started watching McAfee on our phones instead. 30 media members. Watching Rodgers shred McCarthy. A few minutes into Rodgers’ diatribe, McCarthy comes walking through all of us to head upstairs after practice. Everyone listening to multiple phones on full volume. I was here for AB’s helicopter. I was here for the Anthem-debacle presser. Tomlin’s presser wandering onto the field in Baltimore. The players ripping Harrison after he went to New England. The players raiding LeV Bell’s locker for his cleats during his contract dispute. Cowher’s jaw-jutting “GIVE ME A NAME, don’t give me ‘sources'” at that reporter who asked about Kordell. I’ve covered the Steelers for 25 years. I’ve never seen anything like this before. — Tim Benz (@TimBenzPGH) November 25, 2026 And while Ted Mosby may have needed nine seasons to finish his story, nobody in that lobby was willing to let a sitcom rerun cost them a minute of what Rodgers was saying. The reporters pulled up the broadcast on their own phones instead, and before long several of them were blaring Rodgers’ interview at full volume across the lobby. Roughly 10 minutes after practice wrapped, with Rodgers still in the thick of his monologue, Mike McCarthy emerged and strode straight through the middle of that cacophony on his way upstairs, per ESPN’s Brooke Pryor . PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh , who ranked the moment among the strangest sights of his reporting career, noted that McCarthy looked visibly displeased as he passed through. He had good reason, because the voice filling the lobby — and permeating the locker room — belonged to a quarterback he had benched less than 24 hours earlier. Late Tuesday night, only hours after McCarthy had publicly stood by Rodgers following a listless offensive showing against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Steelers announced that their quarterback would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and that Mason Rudolph would start in his place. item.content:encoded: Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Aaron Rodgers spent Wednesday afternoon savaging Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show , and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ best attempt to keep the spectacle out of their own building amounted to changing the channel. According to Tim Benz , who has covered the team for 25 years, about 30 media members waiting for the post-practice locker room session had gathered around a television in the facility’s lobby, transfixed by Rodgers’ ESPN appearance, until a team staffer came through and flipped the channel to How I Met Your Mother . To corroborate this, we were all waiting to go into the locker room after practice. We were watching Rodgers on @PatMcAfeeShow on a TV in the lobby. A team staffer came through and changed the channel to “How I Met Your Mother.” So we all just started watching McAfee on our phones instead. 30 media members. Watching Rodgers shred McCarthy. A few minutes into Rodgers’ diatribe, McCarthy comes walking through all of us to head upstairs after practice. Everyone listening to multiple phones on full volume. I was here for AB’s helicopter. I was here for the Anthem-debacle presser. Tomlin’s presser wandering onto the field in Baltimore. The players ripping Harrison after he went to New England. The players raiding LeV Bell’s locker for his cleats during his contract dispute. Cowher’s jaw-jutting “GIVE ME A NAME, don’t give me ‘sources'” at that reporter who asked about Kordell. I’ve covered the Steelers for 25 years. I’ve never seen anything like this before. — Tim Benz (@TimBenzPGH) November 25, 2026 And while Ted Mosby may have needed nine seasons to finish his story, nobody in that lobby was willing to let a sitcom rerun cost them a minute of what Rodgers was saying. The reporters pulled up the broadcast on their own phones instead, and before long several of them were blaring Rodgers’ interview at full volume across the lobby. Roughly 10 minutes after practice wrapped, with Rodgers still in the thick of his monologue, Mike McCarthy emerged and strode straight through the middle of that cacophony on his way upstairs, per ESPN’s Brooke Pryor . PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh , who ranked the moment among the strangest sights of his reporting career, noted that McCarthy looked visibly displeased as he passed through. He had good reason, because the voice filling the lobby — and permeating the locker room — belonged to a quarterback he had benched less than 24 hours earlier. Late Tuesday night, only hours after McCarthy had publicly stood by Rodgers following a listless offensive showing against the Philadelphia Eagles , the Steelers announced that their quarterback would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos and that Mason Rudolph would start in his place. Rodgers told McAfee that word of the benching reached him through tight end Pat Freiermuth rather than his head coach, and that slight became the starting point for an extraordinary account of his relationship with the man who coached him for 13 seasons in Green Bay. By Rodgers’ telling, McCarthy had been dozing off and snoring through meetings and skipping walk-throughs, and he insisted the coach had brought those habits with him from Green Bay. He said he had confronted McCarthy about them for months as a concerned friend. As the Steelers’ offense floundered, Rodgers said those talks shifted to the play calling, which he wanted McCarthy to hand over to someone else, and he eventually spelled out what he expected to happen if the coach wouldn’t. “If you try and bench me or don’t change the play calling, then you should just release me.” A year ago, Rodgers wasn’t appearing on McAfee’s show at all, as the weekly segments that reliably manufactured headlines throughout his years in Green Bay and New York went dark during his first season in Pittsburgh , apparently in deference to Mike Tomlin. Tomlin’s departure instantly revived the question of whether those appearances would return under McCarthy , and Rodgers answered before he had even committed to another season, returning to McAfee’s show in the spring as a pending free agent to discuss his undecided future and his new head coach. Once he signed on for a 22nd season and reported to training camp, the familiar spectacle returned in full. By the time McAfee broadcast live from Latrobe this summer, the quarterback felt emboldened enough to devote his airtime to a broadside against Anthony Fauci , and McCarthy, asked about the episode the following day , showed little appetite for the furor his quarterback had stirred up. “But at the end of the day, my job is to keep it about football, keep the focus on winning,” McCarthy said at the time. That aspiration proved far easier to articulate than to enforce once the games began. Following a Week 3 loss to the New England Patriots, Rodgers accepted responsibility for the sputtering offense at the postgame podium before pivoting to his coach and insinuating that McCarthy needed a keener understanding of what was working so the Steelers could call better plays. Mike Florio saw through the veneer of accountability and condemned it as open disrespect of McCarthy , likening the remarks to Rodgers’ grievances about lethargic sideline energy during their final seasons together in Green Bay and grouping them with his McAfee and Cam Heyward podcast appearances as part of a persistent campaign of passive-aggressive jabs. As it turns out, Rodgers brought back the same concerns about McCarthy’s engagement that he once raised about the energy on Green Bay’s sideline, this time in an airing of grievances that will almost certainly end his NFL career. Rodgers has long insisted he has no interest in television , and the networks reportedly have little interest in him , so there’s no obvious second act waiting for him in the media either. That leaves McAfee’s show as one of the few places still willing to let Rodgers tell his side of the story, and after Wednesday, it might be the only one. The post Mike McCarthy walked past Steelers reporters listening to Aaron Rodgers rip him on ‘The Pat McAfee Show’ appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Will Kyle Whittingham be fired if Ohio State beats Michigan? What to know
item.description: The high point of Michigan 's season to date came when it upset UCLA on Nov. 21. But the Wolverines have not had many other high points this season, so if Michigan can't win The Game on Nov. 28, will head coach Kyle Whittingham keep his job? Michigan is 6-5 record and a loss in The Game would give UM its first six-loss season since 2014, when coach Brady Hoke was fired. A few days prior, Hoke had fallen to Ohio State coach Urban Meyer, marking Meyer's third win in the Michigan game 42-28. Whittingham is a descendant of Meyer's coaching tree. He spent 32 seasons on Utah's coaching staff, including as Meyer's defensive coordinator. Whittingham was the head coach of Utah for 21 seasons. Ohio State is also experiencing rare setbacks. The Buckeyes are 7-4 and likely out of the College Football Playoff after losing to unranked Nebraska on Sept. 21. Read about what went wrong for the Wolverines below. What is Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham's contract buyout? Michigan hired Whittingham on Dec. 26, 2025, shortly after firing previous head coach Sherrone Moore. Whittingham signed a five-year, $41 million contract, according to records obtained by the Detroit Free Press . If UM relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement," per the Detroit Free Press. He's set to be paid $33.0 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout now would cost $24.75 million. What went wrong with Michigan's season? The Wolverines' season took a turn for the worse almost immediately. In the season opener against MAC opponent Western Michigan , Michigan was down 12-7 as the clock ticked toward zero. The Wolverines unsuccessfully attempted a Hail Mary play. The game, however, didn't end. The booth ordered a second back on the clock, despite the fact that the NBC broadcast clock had expired. Underwood then completed a 47-yard game-winning pass to JJ Buchanan. Although the MAC appealed the game's outcome, the FBS oversight committee stated it lacked the authority to overturn it. “The committee consulted with national officiating leadership regarding the instant replay protocols,” the NCAA statement reads in part. “Based on that information, the committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest’s second-to-last play. Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different.” Their first win stained, more trouble ensued for the Wolverines, who won their first two conference games but lost their first two Big Ten games to Iowa and Minnesota. Halfway through Michigan's next game against Penn State Oct. 17, the team benched Underwood after he threw two interceptions in the first half. item.content:encoded: The high point of Michigan 's season to date came when it upset UCLA on Nov. 21. But the Wolverines have not had many other high points this season, so if Michigan can't win The Game on Nov. 28, will head coach Kyle Whittingham keep his job? Michigan is 6-5 record and a loss in The Game would give UM its first six-loss season since 2014, when coach Brady Hoke was fired. A few days prior, Hoke had fallen to Ohio State coach Urban Meyer, marking Meyer's third win in the Michigan game 42-28. Whittingham is a descendant of Meyer's coaching tree. He spent 32 seasons on Utah's coaching staff, including as Meyer's defensive coordinator. Whittingham was the head coach of Utah for 21 seasons. Ohio State is also experiencing rare setbacks. The Buckeyes are 7-4 and likely out of the College Football Playoff after losing to unranked Nebraska on Sept. 21. Read about what went wrong for the Wolverines below. What is Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham's contract buyout? Michigan hired Whittingham on Dec. 26, 2025, shortly after firing previous head coach Sherrone Moore. Whittingham signed a five-year, $41 million contract, according to records obtained by the Detroit Free Press . If UM relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement," per the Detroit Free Press. He's set to be paid $33.0 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout now would cost $24.75 million. What went wrong with Michigan's season? The Wolverines' season took a turn for the worse almost immediately. In the season opener against MAC opponent Western Michigan , Michigan was down 12-7 as the clock ticked toward zero. The Wolverines unsuccessfully attempted a Hail Mary play. The game, however, didn't end. The booth ordered a second back on the clock, despite the fact that the NBC broadcast clock had expired. Underwood then completed a 47-yard game-winning pass to JJ Buchanan. Although the MAC appealed the game's outcome, the FBS oversight committee stated it lacked the authority to overturn it. “The committee consulted with national officiating leadership regarding the instant replay protocols,” the NCAA statement reads in part. “Based on that information, the committee agreed that the instant replay protocols were not followed in the contest’s second-to-last play. Had the protocols been followed, the outcome of the game would have been different.” Their first win stained, more trouble ensued for the Wolverines, who won their first two conference games but lost their first two Big Ten games to Iowa and Minnesota. Halfway through Michigan's next game against Penn State Oct. 17, the team benched Underwood after he threw two interceptions in the first half. Backup quarterback Tommy Carr came onto the field after Michigan received the second-half kickoff and led the Wolverines to a 21-18 comeback win. Carr started the next three games, which included losses to Indiana and Michigan State and a 28-21 win vs. Rutgers. Michigan scored 12 points combined in the two losses and gained fewer than 200 yards in the loss to the Spartans. The Wolverines were also shut out in the first half for the third time this season against MSU, which hadn't happened three times in a season since 1932. Michigan then fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck . "The results have not matched our desired outcome, and I felt that a change in leadership was required for our offense," said Whittingham in a press release. Already at four Big Ten losses, Michigan then played Oregon on Nov. 14. The Ducks were a three-loss team, but coming off a 41-28 beatdown of Ohio State a week prior. Michigan deployed both Carr and Underwood, but the quarterbacks combined for 71 passing yards and completed six of 20 passes. Oregon ended up stomping Michigan 31-7 for the Wolverines' fifth Big Ten loss. Michigan rebounded for an 18-16 triple-overtime win against previously undefeated UCLA on Nov. 21. The Wolverines played Underwood exclusively and he who finished 11 of 24 on passes for 127 yards and a touchdown. He also threw the game-winning two-point conversion to tight end Jalen Hoffman. Will Kyle Whittingham get fired? It's not clear whether Whittingham's job is at risk if the Wolverines drop their sixth game of the season and lose to Ohio State, given Whittingham's massive buyout figure and the fact it's his first year on the job. Michigan is also currently having issues with its higher administration. Michigan athletic director Warde Manuel was expected to step down on Dec. 31 incoming AD Trev Alberts, but the school is no longer hiring Alberts because he did not pass a background check, according to the Detroit Free Press . Manuel will remain with Michigan until the school finds a full-time replacement, per multiple reports. Manuel was expected to step down following an independent investigation of the school's athletic leadership. The investigation came in the aftermath of a series of scandals, including Moore's firing from the program after a relationship with a staffer. This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Will Kyle Whittingham be fired if Ohio State beats Michigan? What to know

item.title: Malachi Moreno not expected to play Friday vs. Wichita State due to concussion
item.description: Following a hard fall last Friday night at Lucas Oil Stadium during Kentucky’s game against Indiana, star center Malachi Moreno is not expected to play Friday night against Wichita State. Moreno did return to the game against Indiana after briefly leaving in the second half, finishing with 12 points and a team-high seven rebounds in 32 minutes. He also was 6/9 from the field and had two blocks. Mark Pope said on Wednesday that he doesn’t expect Moreno to be able to play Friday, with a UK spokesperson saying Moreno is still in the concussion protocol and is progressing but hasn’t resumed practicing. Moreno is currently third on the team in scoring at 13.8 points per game, and he leads the team with 8.7 rebounds per game and 11 blocks. He’s also shooting an efficient 66.7 percent from the floor and playing 27.8 minutes per game. With Moreno not expected to play Friday, the onus is now on Franck Kepnang and Reece Potter to step in and both fill the void. Kentucky-Wichita State will tip off at 9:00 ET on ESPN2 and the UK Sports Network.

item.title: Red Sox Should Only Sign 12-Year Veteran Under One Condition
item.description: Red Sox Should Only Sign 12-Year Veteran Under One Condition originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The one question the Red Sox have to consider with their rotation this year is whether they want to bring in another left-handed starter. With Payton Tolle, Garrett Crochet, and Ranger Suarez already in the rotation, adding another left-hander might not be the best decision. The Red Sox, however, might not view that as a big issue, considering those three guys are among the best in baseball. One could already argue that Crochet is a top-five pitcher in the game; Suarez has been lights-out for a very long time and Tolle looks to be a potential star in the making. If Boston is content with bringing in another left-hander, it will make some easier decisions during the offseason. When recently looking at some players who could be fits, the Red Sox's beat reporter for The Athletic recently suggested another left-hander in Matthew Boyd, the Chicago Cubs free agent who posted a 3.91 ERA last season. “Boyd, a veteran lefty, posted a 3.91 ERA in 22 starts over 126 ⅔ innings for the Chicago Cubs last year while also missing time for a meniscus tear. Over two seasons with the Cubs, he posted a 3.50 ERA, 20.2 percent strikeout rate, 6.5 percent walk rate and 39.7 percent groundball rate. Boyd battled injuries for much of 2021-24, but would still be an intriguing option at the back of Boston’s rotation even as another lefty. MLB Trade Rumors projects a one-year, $13 million deal for Boyd,” Jen McCaffrey of The Athletic wrote. In a perfect world, the Red Sox would bring in a right-hander who can get outs at a high level, even if that's similar to Boyd. At the same time, if Boyd can be had for a somewhat low price and the Red Sox feel fine with how their rotation looks, there are far worse options out there. He's been above average for quite some time now and should be more than fine in a Red Sox rotation that has a chance to be very good if everything goes as planned. item.title: 49ers QB Brock Purdy held out of practice for ankle injury suffered in Mexico City game
item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy talks to Jerry Rice before the game against the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. (Fernando Llano/Associated Press) It doesn't sound like a serious ailment, but it qualifies as a big deal because it involves the health of the San Francisco 49ers ' franchise quarterback: Brock Purdy didn't practice Wednesday because of an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan termed Purdy "day-to-day" after he was injured during the second quarter of the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings last Sunday in Mexico City. Shanahan said Purdy didn't have a high ankle sprain, which typically sidelines players for multiple weeks, and that Purdy's injury didn't impact Shanahan's play-calling after he was checked on the sideline. "They always tell you when someone has (an injury), but then they come back and they're like, ‘Hey, checked out. He should be fine,'" Shanahan said. "He didn't miss any plays." Purdy appeared to be injured with 11 seconds left in the second quarter when defensive tackle Jalen Redmond rolled up on his left ankle while pressuring Purdy on a play in which Purdy was flagged for intentional grounding. Before Purdy was injured, with the 49ers leading 28-10, he completed 12 of 15 passes for 176 yards and three touchdown passes. He then completed 9 of 11 passes for 79 yards. Purdy didn't have a rushing attempt. Shanahan downplayed the seriousness of Purdy's injury, but he declined to definitely say he would start against the Seahawks on Sunday at Levi's Stadium. "I mean, he can't (practice) today, so it's always a possibility," Shanahan said. "… It's day-to-day with it, but we've got to see how it goes." If Purdy is unavailable Sunday, the 49ers would turn to Mac Jones , who has thrown one pass while playing 20 mop-up snaps this season. In 2025, Jones went 5-3 as a fill-in starter when Purdy was sidelined with turf toe and ranked second in the NFL in completion percentage (69.6%). item.title: UIL playoff predictions 2026: Picks for Lake Travis vs Brennan, Round Rock and more
item.description: The Lake Travis Cavaliers celebrate becoming Area Champions and advancing in the playoffs after beating Cibolo Steele in overtime at Rattler Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 20, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) UIL playoff football is in full swing in Central Texas . The American-Statesman's seasonlong staff picks for the week's top Austin-area matchups feature high school reporters Colby Gordon and Shaun Chornobroff , high school correspondent Jay Plotkin and sports editor Richard Tijerina . Gordon is our defending champion. The first two rounds of the postseason provided plenty of excitement, including down-to-the-wire victories by Lake Travis and Weiss last week. The regional semifinals should provide similar thrills. MORE : 16 underrated Austin-area players thriving in postseaso n Here are some Austin-area matchups that have caught our eye this Friday: Cibolo Steele Knights defensive back Michael Johnson III (12) attempts to bring down Lake Travis Cavaliers wide receiver Gray Garrick (11) in the second quarter of the area-round playoff game between the Lake Travis Cavaliers and Cibolo Steele Knights at Rattler Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 20, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) Lake Travis vs. San Antonio Brennan There may not have been a better game in Texas last week than the overtime matchup between Lake Travis and Cibolo Steele, a contest the Cavaliers (7-3-1) won 39-38. It was a remarkable comeback from a Lake Travis team that received explosive plays from both its defense and special teams in a true team win. Those units will have to make an impact again Friday when the Cavs take on San Antonio Brennan at Texas State. Brennan (11-1) is led by four-star running back Jayshawn Mitchell, who has run for 1,306 yards and 28 touchdowns this season. The Bears have also allowed just 81 points this season. It will be another difficult tilt for the Cavs. But this team showed in its last contest that it can find a way to win those. RELATED: Lake Travis' gamble pays off as 2-point conversion gives it OT win Chornobroff's Pick: Lake Travis 27, Brennan 21 Weiss vs. A&M Consolidated The last time these two teams met, A&M Consolidated notched a 49-47 road win over Weiss. However, Weiss rebounded and won the district, while a late-season stumble by Consol pushed it down to the No. 4 seed in the final standings. Still, the Tigers bounced region favorite Richmond Randle, led by Texas commit running back Landon Williams-Callis, in the bi-district round and beat Goose Creek Memorial by 17 last week. Weiss cruised to a 56-7 win over Iowa Colony in the bi-district round and beat Port Arthur Memorial 28-26 on a 94-yard Jordan Anderson kickoff return in the area round. Chornorboff's Pick: Weiss 35, A&M Consolidated 32 MORE: Talented Hutto seniors bid farewell after Katy loss Waco La Vega vs. Wimberley Two of the best teams in Class 4A Division II meet Friday when Waco La Vega (12-0) faces Wimberley (11-0). La Vega is the top-ranked team in 4A

item.title: Daniel Dubois and Joseph Parker Added to 2027 Boxing Schedule
item.description: What To Know Two years after it was originally scheduled, the heavyweight title fight between Daniel Dubois and Joseph Parker has been set for the 2027 boxing schedule. Dubois vs Parker will take place on January 30 at the Co-op Arena in Manchester, England. The fight will be for higher stakes as Dubois is coming off two knockout wins over Fabio Wardley, with the first fight the likely 2026 Fight of the Year Daniel Dubois was set to defend the IBF World Heavyweight title for the second time against Joseph Parker on February 22, 2025, as part of the “New Year’s Retribution” card from Queensberry Promotions in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The matchup was scheduled as the co-main event in support of the rematch between undisputed light heavyweight champion Artur Beterbiev and Dmitry Bivol. But it never took place. Queensberry Promotions announced that Daniel Dubois would defend his title against Joseph Parker on January 30 in Manchester, England. Photo: Queensberry Promotions Finally, the matchup has been resurrected. Queensberry Promotions announced that Dubois vs Parker will finally take place on January 30 at the Co-op Arena in Manchester, England, dubbed “New Year’s Retribution.” Promoter Frank Warren calls it a bigger fight than ever, pointing out that Dubois is in prime form after two stoppage wins over Fabio Wardley. Parker adds the drama in his quest to reclaim the WBO title he once held. It had to happen… 👊 Daniel Dubois and Joseph Parker get their chance to handle business in Manchester 🔥 #DuboisParker | Jan 30 | Co-op Live, Manchester | DAZN https://t.co/EcIxZoxtx0 — Queensberry Promotions (@Queensberry) November 25, 2026 The Long Road to Dubois vs Parker in 2027 At the time of the original fight, Dubois was angling for a rematch against Oleksandr Usyk. He considered Parker a mere stepping stone. “This is show business, so that’s who I want next. First I gotta get through this guy (Parker). I’m gonna do a demolition job on him first, and then I want Usyk next. I’m ready for it, and I’m on a roll. So, bring him on.” The comments didn’t sit too well with Parker, who was coming off upset victories over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang in his two previous fights. The former WBO heavyweight champion assured Dubois that he wasn’t one to be overlooked. “You might be looking too far ahead,” replied Parker. “Planning big fights, other big fights. You’ve got a fight right in front of you, right now.” Here’s how things were going down at the time. Can you count how many times they told each other to “shut up” ? 😭 Dubois had no interest in a handshake 🌶️ #DuboisParker | Jan | Live Exclusively on DAZN 🤳 https://t.co/jPZyO2p5y2 — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) November 25, 2026 Dubois Out – Martin Bakole to the Rescue Joseph Parker faced Martin Bakole instead of Daniel Dubois, stopping him in two rounds to win the WBO interim heavyweight title. on February 23, 2025. Parker adds the drama in his quest to reclaim the WBO title he once held. It had to happen… 👊 Daniel Dubois and Joseph Parker get their chance to handle business in Manchester 🔥 #DuboisParker | Jan 30 | Co-op Live, Manchester | DAZN https://t.co/EcIxZoxtx0 — Queensberry Promotions (@Queensberry) November 25, 2026 The Long Road to Dubois vs Parker in 2027 At the time of the original fight, Dubois was angling for a rematch against Oleksandr Usyk. He considered Parker a mere stepping stone. “This is show business, so that’s who I want next. First I gotta get through this guy (Parker). I’m gonna do a demolition job on him first, and then I want Usyk next. I’m ready for it, and I’m on a roll. So, bring him on.” The comments didn’t sit too well with Parker, who was coming off upset victories over Deontay Wilder and Zhilei Zhang in his two previous fights. The former WBO heavyweight champion assured Dubois that he wasn’t one to be overlooked. “You might be looking too far ahead,” replied Parker. “Planning big fights, other big fights. You’ve got a fight right in front of you, right now.” Here’s how things were going down at the time. Can you count how many times they told each other to “shut up” ? 😭 Dubois had no interest in a handshake 🌶️ #DuboisParker | Jan | Live Exclusively on DAZN 🤳 https://t.co/jPZyO2p5y2 — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) November 25, 2026 Dubois Out – Martin Bakole to the Rescue Joseph Parker faced Martin Bakole instead of Daniel Dubois, stopping him in two rounds to win the WBO interim heavyweight title. on February 23, 2025. Photo: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing But the matchup fell apart just days before the fight card when Dubois fell ill and withdrew due to illness. This set up a whirlwind effort to find Parker a replacement opponent, resulting in a deal with Martin Bakole. Bakole took the fight on two days’ notice and hopped on an Ethiopian Airlines flight the day before from his native Congo, barely making it to Riyadh at 2 a.m. on the day of the fight. The move turned Bakole into an instant boxing folk hero. Parker didn’t hesitate to say yes to the replacement opponent despite Bakole’s impressive performance in August against Jared Anderson. Credit to Bakole for seizing the opportunity. But he was admittedly not in the greatest shape. Parker defanged several big punchers in his career, including Derek Chisora, Andy Ruiz Jr., Zhilei Zhang, and Deontay Wilder. Bakole became another, as Parker scored a second-round knockout win. Joseph Parker Stumbles Parker was riding high, and next he took on Fabio Wardley. Things didn’t go as well for Parker, who lost by an 11th-round TKO to Wardley in October 2025. Following the loss, Parker received a three-month suspension after testing positive for a cocaine metabolite. Parker denied knowingly using the drug. UK Anti-Doping (UKAD) accepted his claim that the substance entered his system out-of-competition via food contaminated by his nutritionist. Parker’s provisional ban ended in August 2026 and Parker was cleared to return to the ring in August 2026. It’s one of boxing’s ironies that Bakole will be back in the ring himself, once again as a late replacement opponent against Deontay Wilder on the Fury vs Joshua undercard on December 5. Bakole was already scheduled to fight Solomon Adebayo of Nigeria. He has been in training camp, and there are no last-minute travel issues. Dubois vs Parker: Worthy Matchup Parker remains a top heavyweight with a solid resume. He’s been a sparring partner for virtually all the British heavyweights through the years, including Tyson Fury. He’s well-liked and outgoing, known for creative music videos produced with his friend and videographer/director Kevin Kelley, often starring his family and friends. Dubois is such a stoic personality. Parker’s participation in pre-fight promotional antics will be a welcome addition. Here’s hoping he puts together something new. His last video was a callout of Oleksandr Usyk a year ago, and he’s still the one.

item.content:encoded: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 24: Isiah Harwell #1 of the Gonzaga Bulldogs reacts during the first half against the Kansas State Wildcats during the Players Era 16 bracket of The 2026 Players Era Men's Championship at T-Mobile Arena on November 24, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Players Era/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a dominant 40-point victory over the Kansas State Wildcats, the No. 22 Gonzaga Bulldogs (4-1) will face off against the Baylor Bears (5-1) in the second of potentially four rounds in the Players Era 16 Tournament in Las Vegas. The game will tip off bright and early for basketball fans, with an 8:30 pm P.T. start time, streaming live on ESPN. The unranked Bears have been one of the most under-the-radar teams in the country so far this season, coming off a five-point win over the No. 15 Alabama Crimson Tide in the game that ended right before Gonzaga tipped off. After beating the Florida Gators and Illinois Fighting Illini in exhibitions before the season, the No. 1 and No. 3 ranked preseason teams in the country, Baylor’s only loss of the season has come at the hands of the No. 7 Texas Longhorns by three points in San Antonio. Gonzaga moved up to No. 11 in KenPom’s rankings, while the site has Baylor ranked at No. 24. The Bears and Bulldogs have met twice since the 2021 national championship game that Zags fans want to forget, and this will be the first meeting since the 2024 season-opener that Bears fans want to forget (albeit VJ Edgecombe’s baptism of Joe Few). But, much like back in 2021, Baylor comes in with a stout defense going up against a Gonzaga offense that found its groove in last night’s contest. Scouting Baylor The Bears have allowed just 62.0 points per game defensively this season, and stymied a high-paced Crimson Tide offense that’s been the M.O. of coach Nate Oats’ game plan. Alabama shot just 34.5% from the floor and 23.3% from three, and while Baylor also struggled (33.33% from the field), the defense did enough to win the clunky affair, which ended in a 68-63 final. Meanwhile, the Zags used a balanced offensive attack to run away from Kansas State and put up 101 points in the win. It will be a test for coach Mark Few’s offense against one of the country’s more athletic perimeter defenses under coach Scott Drew. For the Bears, brothers Kayden (15.7 points per game) and Dylan Mingo (13.0 points per game) lead a guard- and forward-heavy offensive attack, while Liberty Flames transfer Brett Decker Jr. (15.2 points per game, 47% from deep) has been having a hot start to the year. Kayden Mingo led the way with 19 points in the win over Alabama. This game will be a test for Gonzaga’s guards, as each of Baylor’s top seven scorers is 6-foot-7 or under. However, this again plays into the hands of Massamba Diop, Braden Huff, and Izan Almansa. Diop (18 points) had his best game as a Zag against Kansas State, and will look to continue his momentum into a game where he should be matched up with undersized defenders. Baylor center Justin Bodo Bodo will have his work cut out for him, but the 6-foot-10 center has only averaged 15 minutes per game and could see an increase to compensate for the Zags’ talented frontcourt. Despite the size disadvantage, Gonzaga will have to focus on rebounding, as Baylor is first in the Big 12 in offensive rebounds per game (17.0) and second in total rebounds per game (41.7). The Bears will be feisty on the perimeter and on the glass and will present a challenge to the Zags in the trenches. Keys to the Game Gonzaga could play four games in a five-day stretch during Feast Week, but this day off before what should be a physical game against Baylor will be crucial. The size advantage for the Zags is incredibly misleading for this game, as the Bears are going to crash the boards early and often in this game. Although Baylor hasn’t been shooting well from beyond the arc to begin the year (34.5%), Gonzaga needs to find Decker Jr. around the perimeter. The LSU Tigers hadn’t been shooting well from three to start the year, and in the one-point loss to coach Will Wade in Spokane previously on Nov. 14, the Zags couldn’t rebound and guard the three-point line down the stretch. In a way, this is a get-right game in the rebounding and perimeter defense department for Gonzaga, who needs to show that they learned from the heartbreaking loss to LSU. Xaivian Lee, Isiah Harwell, and Nathan De Sousa were great in the opening Kansas State matchup, and with Javon Bennett (knee sprain) out for at least a couple of weeks, these three will continue to run the show in the backcourt. The frontcourt will be on display again in this game, as Diop and Huff will need to dominate the paint to throw Baylor off their rhythm. Davis Fogle (nine points) failed to reach double digits in scoring against Kansas State, but looked smooth offensively and didn’t need to have a juggernaut performance to push the Zags to a win. A calm and composed Fogle against Baylor’s tenacious perimeter defense will be a great test for the NBA-hopeful wing. This matchup will fly under the radar in Feast Week, but with Baylor playing its best basketball in a long time and Gonzaga looking fresh after their week off, fireworks could come from this 2021 rematch back in Indianapolis. Few and Drew are very familiar with each other, and this will be another installment in the two legendary coaches’ careers.

item.title: Xavier Musketeers hold off Texas A&M for big Bahamas win
item.description: NASSAU, Bahamas - After a promising start to the season gave way to a frustrating two-game homestand that included an 18-point loss to Iowa, Xavier arrived in the Bahamas with questions to answer and an opportunity to change the conversation surrounding their season. In need of a response, Xavier found one on Wednesday, Nov. 25 by knocking off undefeated Texas A&M , 88-83, in the opening round of the Signature Series of the Battle 4 Atlantis at Imperial Arena. The Musketeers got a much-needed bounce-back victory, and an early-season resume boost against a team that was one spot away from being ranked in the latest AP Top 25 poll. More: Xavier vs. Texas A&M start delayed for roof leak in Bahamas More: Bold predictions for Xavier vs. Texas A&M at Battle 4 Atlantis The victory was especially important for a Xavier team that had seen some of its early momentum disappear during a difficult week at home. The Musketeers needed to scratch and claw for a 75-67 victory over Cleveland State before Iowa took the wind out of Xavier’s sails on its home floor. With Richard Pitino saying Xavier needed to do some “soul-searching,” his team found it in paradise with a decisive performance against a Texas A&M squad that entered the event averaging nearly 100 points per game. Xavier trailed for less than 90 seconds overall and led by as many as 18 in the second half before Texas A&M came storming back to tie it in the final minute of regulation. Despite another tough night at the charity stripe, Xavier hit five free throws in the final 35 seconds and did enough on the defensive end to get a marquee non-conference win. Xavier got a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double from Mike Nwoko, who hit the go-ahead free throws with 35 seconds left. Xavier shot 47.5% overall and had Tru Washington (15) and Gabriel Pozzato (14) in double figures, as well. In his first collegiate start, freshman Kalek House had nine points, four assists and three rebounds. The Musketeers (6-1) now turn their attention to another major opportunity on Friday, Nov. 27, when they face No. 2 Virginia at 11 a.m. A victory over the Cavaliers could potentially transform the outlook of Xavier’s season in a matter of days with back-to-back wins that will hold weight all the way to March. This article originally appeared on Cincinnati Enquirer: Xavier Musketeers hold off Texas A&M for big Bahamas win

item.title: 76ers’ LeBron James feeling himself after showing limitless range on 3-pointer vs. Heat
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 76ers’ LeBron James feeling himself after showing limitless range on 3-pointer vs. Heat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Nick Nurse ’s Philadelphia 76ers welcomed the Miami Heat to Philly on Wednesday, November 25 as Nurse commented on a health issue facing Joel Embiid lately . Heat coach Erik Spoelstra had a bold comment on his former player James’ battle against Father Time that raised eyebrows. The 76ers set the drama aside as they took a late second quarter lead against the Heat in NBA Cup Group Stage action at Xfinity Mobile Arena. James put the Sixers up six points with a dagger three not far from the gold NBA Cup trophy logo as he showed off his nearly limitless range on the basketball court. LEBRON JAMES FROM WAY OUTSIDE 😳 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Sixers lead the Heat 45-39. pic.twitter.com/UeolVBIyR7 — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 25, 2026 James led the Sixers with 16 points in 17 minutes, followed by Tyrese Maxey ’s 15 points in 15 minutes, as the Sixers protected a two-point lead headed toward halftime. Coach Nurse’s team entered the halftime locker rooms up 62-53 as Maxey pushed his total to 17 points. The Heat got 16 first-half points from Giannis Antetokounmpo and 12 from Davion Mitchell, while Klay Thompson had just five points against the Sixers on the road. Nurse’s team knocked down 7-of-14 three-pointers in the first half, shooting their way to a solid lead without Embiid in the lineup against a 10-6 Miami team. James and his family have been busy both on and off the court lately as his wife Savannah filed a restraining order against two alleged stalkers recently . LeBron James appeared ready to blow off some steam on the court as he helped shoot down the Heat in the first half, much to the delight of the 76ers faithful on a cold fall night in Philly. item.title: Wisconsin Badgers vs. Northeastern Huskies Game Thread: Get Right Game?
item.description: PORTLAND, OREGON - MARCH 19: Head coach Greg Gard of the Wisconsin Badgers watches while playing the High Point Panthers during the second half in the first round of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament at Moda Center on March 19, 2026 in Portland, Oregon. The Panthers won 83-82 in regulation. (Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a disappointing week at the Baha Mar Championship, the Wisconsin Badgers are facing off against the Northeastern Huskies back at the Kohl Center, with tip-off set for 6:00 p.m. on Big Ten Network. Wisconsin’s season took another rough turn last week, as they lost 74-69 to Seton Hall before getting blown out 70-53 to Murray State in the third-place game. In both games, the Badgers saw huge deficits in the first half that they weren’t able to overcome. To make matters worse, Wisconsin lost senior reserve guard Jack Janicki for the season due to a foot injury in the Murray State game. Now, head coach Greg Gard will need to figure out his rotation, which he’s tinkered with a bit already in the first six games of the season. Now, Wisconsin takes on Northeastern on Wednesday evening, and they’re 20.5-point favorites heading into the game. The Badgers have now been 20+ point favorites in five of their seven games so far, but have covered in only one of the first four, with all of their other wins coming by single digits. Northeastern has started the year 2-4 with losses to Boston, Virginia, Butler, and Stonehill. They’ve allowed 90+ points in three games, while also giving up 84 points to Butler. This feels like a potential get-right game for the Badgers, but they’ve also underwhelmed against opponents they’ve been heavily favored over so far this season. Can Wisconsin rebound with a strong performance on Wednesday? Join us as our game thread is officially open!

item.title: Report: Kevin Gausman Agrees to One-Year Deal with Tigers
item.description: Sep 30, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; Chicago Cubs pitcher Kevin Gausman (12) delivers a pitch in the first inning against the San Diego Padres during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory … | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Augustus Oswald, Site Editor Right-handed starting pitcher Kevin Gausman has agreed to a one-year contract with the Detroit Tigers, according to ESPN’s Jeff Passan. The contract is worth $25 million for the 2027 season. Aug 18, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Cubs pitcher Kevin Gausman (12) pitches against the Chicago White Sox during the first inning at Wrigley Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Kevin Gausman’s 2026 Season Gausman, 35, split last season between the Toronto Blue Jays and Chicago Cubs. In 32 starts between the two teams, Gausman went 9-12 with a 4.51 ERA. The Cubs acquired the Colorado native at the trade deadline to bolster their rotation. He was serviceable down the stretch, posting a 4-2 record with a 4.83 ERA. Right-hander Kevin Gausman and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a one-year, $25 million contract, pending physical, sources tell ESPN. Gausman, 35, is one of the best workhorses in baseball, with the second-most innings of any pitcher since 2021. — Jeff Passan (@JeffPassan) November 25, 2026 Gausman’s Career So Far This will be Gausman’s 15th year in the major leagues. He is joining his seventh team. His longest tenure with an organization was with the Baltimore Orioles, where he pitched from 2013-2018. He has also played for the Atlanta Braves, Cincinnati Reds , San Francisco Giants , Blue Jays, and Cubs. He has had multiple standout seasons. His first came in 2021, when he won 14 games and helped the Giants win 107 games (a franchise record) and the National League West Division title. He finished sixth in Cy Young voting that season. With the Blue Jays, Gausman finished third in Cy Young voting in 2023 and posted 14 wins in 2024. In 2025, he helped the Blue Jays reach the World Series by posting a 2.93 ERA in six appearances. The Last Word The Tigers are getting a pitcher who is the definition of reliable. Kevin Gausman may not be an ace at this point, but he can be an effective middle-of-the-rotation starter. The Tigers can count on 30+ starts from Gausman. Perhaps Gausman’s most valuable asset is his ability to work deep into games. In a league where managers are not hesitant to go to their bullpen, Gausman can provide a cushion for the Tigers’ bullpen. This is a solid addition for the Tigers. Kevin Gausman won’t move the needle as an ace, but he adds needed durability to the rotation. This is a smart investment for a team looking to return to October and make some noise. More Baseball News: Report: Foster Griffin Re-Signs with Guardians Report: JoJo Romero Signs with Padres Mets Should Target Michael King in Free Agency Main Photo Credit: Denis Poroy- Imagn Images

item.title: Move over, pickleball – Padel elbows into Southwest Florida club scene
item.description: Many country clubs and communities have diversified their offerings in Southwest Florida . We wrote earlier this decade about how pickleball was key to their strategies . Now another sport with a paddle is becoming part of the game plan as we move into 2027 . The hottest amenity drawing attention is padel, a fast-growing racquet activity that blends elements of tennis, squash and other sports and has become one of the newest status symbols at private clubs around the country. Padel is pronounced "pah-DEL" rather than like the word "paddle." For sure, the Sunshine State's country clubs are no longer competing solely on golf courses, clubhouses and dining rooms as part of their business models. And padel, which originated in Mexico in 1969 and slowly started as a niche in Spain and Argentina, is now bouncing into the formula. Here's what to know about padelistas invading Southwest Florida. Where did padel show up this month in Naples, Florida for the first time? At Quail Creek Country Club in North Naples this month, members officially opened their glass-walled three-court padel complex and touted the activity's introduction to Southwest Florida private clubs. They see it as part of a larger shift in how residents and others want to spend their time while saying it puts Quail Creek on the forefront of the global social-sport movement, bringing the activity to Naples and the region. "We're fostering a thriving community around this kinetic sport," Quail Creek General Manager Chris Evans said. “We couldn’t have accomplished this without the vision and leadership of our director of court sports, Jose Pastrello. He has been a champion of the sport, the project, our club and of Naples." Besides padel, what other offerings are included at the Quail Creek CC? It joins tennis, pickleball and bocce as part of an expanding menu of recreational offerings designed to appeal to multiple generations of residents in the Valewood Drive community. So how did it happen at Quail Creek? Where did the inspiration to get padel to Naples, Florida? Was it Miami? Pastrello is president of the Florida Division of the Racquet Sports Professionals Association known as RSPA, which has been discussing the sport. “I was first inspired to bring padel to Naples through our RSPA meetings," Pastrello said. "I was hearing how successful it’s been at other clubs, and after a visit with some Quail Creek members to a club in Miami, I knew right away that our member community would embrace the challenge and social quality of padel." 'Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis' It's the right match for the community, Pastrello said. “Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis, while still being easy to learn,” he said. "I am beyond thrilled to introduce it here. I have so much energy for the sport." What is padel and when and where was it first introduced in the U.S.? item.content:encoded: Many country clubs and communities have diversified their offerings in Southwest Florida . We wrote earlier this decade about how pickleball was key to their strategies . Now another sport with a paddle is becoming part of the game plan as we move into 2027 . The hottest amenity drawing attention is padel, a fast-growing racquet activity that blends elements of tennis, squash and other sports and has become one of the newest status symbols at private clubs around the country. Padel is pronounced "pah-DEL" rather than like the word "paddle." For sure, the Sunshine State's country clubs are no longer competing solely on golf courses, clubhouses and dining rooms as part of their business models. And padel, which originated in Mexico in 1969 and slowly started as a niche in Spain and Argentina, is now bouncing into the formula. Here's what to know about padelistas invading Southwest Florida. Where did padel show up this month in Naples, Florida for the first time? At Quail Creek Country Club in North Naples this month, members officially opened their glass-walled three-court padel complex and touted the activity's introduction to Southwest Florida private clubs. They see it as part of a larger shift in how residents and others want to spend their time while saying it puts Quail Creek on the forefront of the global social-sport movement, bringing the activity to Naples and the region. "We're fostering a thriving community around this kinetic sport," Quail Creek General Manager Chris Evans said. “We couldn’t have accomplished this without the vision and leadership of our director of court sports, Jose Pastrello. He has been a champion of the sport, the project, our club and of Naples." Besides padel, what other offerings are included at the Quail Creek CC? It joins tennis, pickleball and bocce as part of an expanding menu of recreational offerings designed to appeal to multiple generations of residents in the Valewood Drive community. So how did it happen at Quail Creek? Where did the inspiration to get padel to Naples, Florida? Was it Miami? Pastrello is president of the Florida Division of the Racquet Sports Professionals Association known as RSPA, which has been discussing the sport. “I was first inspired to bring padel to Naples through our RSPA meetings," Pastrello said. "I was hearing how successful it’s been at other clubs, and after a visit with some Quail Creek members to a club in Miami, I knew right away that our member community would embrace the challenge and social quality of padel." 'Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis' It's the right match for the community, Pastrello said. “Padel has the energy of pickleball, and the technical aspects of tennis, while still being easy to learn,” he said. "I am beyond thrilled to introduce it here. I have so much energy for the sport." What is padel and when and where was it first introduced in the U.S.? Played on an enclosed court roughly two-thirds the size of a traditional tennis court, the sport combines elements of tennis, squash, racquetball and, to some observers, pickleball. Players use solid perforated rackets and can play the ball off the surrounding glass and mesh walls, creating longer rallies and a highly social atmosphere, according to the International Padel Federation, known as FIP. It was first introduced in the U.S. in 1993 by Argentine native Felipe Arnold and his business partner Ed Thompson at the Houstonian Hotel Club and Spa, according to USA Padel, the national governing body recognized by FIP. More: New $350 million waterfront community coming to East Naples How many play padel in the United States? What major event this week? The annual report from USA Padel shows its membership has blown up from 500 in 2022 to nearly 3,000 in 2025. In that time, its number of U.S. clubs has grown from 30 to more than 100. But the actual American number of Padel participants just exceeded more than a million for the first time, according to Sports & Fitness Industry Association's 2026 sport involvement study. About a quarter of them played at least eight times in a year's time. USA Padel's national team of 56 male and female players ages 35 and more are in Paraguay right now for the Senior Pan American Championship 2026. Last week, its U.S. National Women’s Absolute Team finished 11th place at the FIP World Cup 2026 in Qatar, a four-spot leap from its 15th-place two years ago. Earlier this month, the men landed 13th as they did in 2024. How many play the sport of padel worldwide, and in how many countries? FIP says the sport now has more than 40 million players worldwide and is played in more than 190 countries and territories. The organization reported court construction worldwide has continued to grow at double-digit rates annually. That has received the attention of Florida country clubs like Quail Creek looking to widen their scope beyond golf by adding pickleball, wellness centers, social clubs and new dining venues in an effort to attract younger members, create activities that appeal to entire families and provide year-round engagement for residents and seasonal members. What new connection did padel have to the PGA in 2026 in Florida? The latest trend was visible at this year's PGA Show in Orlando, where padel shared floor space for the first time ever with traditional golf equipment and technology. The sport's rapid growth has become especially noticeable in Florida, where private clubs and developers are racing to add courts. Palm Beach County, for one, has a head start on Southwest Florida, which, for example, has a Smash Point racquet site planning a debut next year on Park Meadows Drive in Fort Myers and has a random court here and there, like a local academy that offers it but primarily markets itself for tennis. How is Palm Beach ahead of Southwest Florida on the sport of padel? Famed The Breakers tennis center expanded last year to include padel. Boca Raton was opening Wednesday what its developers say is Florida's largest indoor pickleball and padel compound , 100,000 square feet of luxury, with each court equipped with cameras and 70-inch monitors allowing players to track scores, replay points and share their plays with coaches and social media. And a new private club on a March completion track with six padel courts, six tennis courts and at least two or so pickleball courts has a waiting list of 700 applicants beyond the 100 original members. Situating it on Billionaire's Row, casino and resort mogul Steve Wynn got the first approval for one in the town of Palm Beach. But it's not been smooth for all padel plutocrats. Palm Beach and neighbors pushed back last month against plans by billionaire Nelson Peltz and his wife to stick a padel court atop a basketball court on his 13-acre oceanfront estate. Earlier this year, the Peltzes — the in-laws of soccer player David Beckham and former Spice Girl Victoria Beckham — ended up having to rip out a previous one they had installed after it sparked a code-violation case . What international soccer superstar is retiring so he can 'play padel?' However, padel's popularity has another soccer superstar contemplating retirement. Cristiano Ronaldo recently revealed plans to potentially retire next year, partly so he can “watch and play padel, which I really like.” And earlier this month, tennis star John McEnroe and golfer Matt Kucher, who also is big into ping pong, played each other in Mexico . Pardoned last year by President Trump after a U.S. insider trading and securities fraud conviction and $50 million federal fine against him and his company, British billionaire and mega Orlando developer Joe Lewis built a 323-foot long superyacht around a padel court in the heart of his $250 million vessel, seen often parked in Fort Lauderdale. item.title: Celtics Reportedly Making Wise Trade Decision on Derrick White Amid Struggles
item.description: Celtics Reportedly Making Wise Trade Decision on Derrick White Amid Struggles originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Celtics have struggled recently, despite still sitting in second place in the Eastern Conference, it's raised questions about what the front office might do before the NBA trade deadline. The Celtics already made one of the biggest moves of the past decade by sending Jaylen Brown to the 76ers in a deal involving Paul George, but as Brad Stevens has shown in the past, when he thinks he has to push buttons, he'll do just that. The Celtics will have an opportunity to improve before the deadline, but as always, it'll come down to what it could cost. According to the latest, despite questions about moving on from players like Derrick White or Sam Hauser, there's no plan to do so, and it would be considered a "shock" if it happened. “Remember, the Celtics came into this season with a focus on staying below the luxury tax and making their move in the offseason. “The losing streak has been unsightly, but it is not going to change the organization from that goal. It would be a shock if players like Derrick White or even Sam Hauser hit the market,” Sean Deveney of Heavy reported . White is a very good player in his own right, but he has slowed down a bit after really impressing in those first couple of years in Boston. The past year or so hasn't been too kind to him as he's taken on a bigger offensive role. This season, perhaps uglier than any other that he's played in Boston, has frankly been inexcusable. It's certainly part of the reason why the Celtics have lost recently, as he's made just three 3-pointers in the last three games on 25 attempts prior to the win against Washington. item.title: In 2026's final MorumBIS clash, Tricolor host Remo in the Brasileirão
item.description: In 2026's final MorumBIS clash, Tricolor host Remo in the Brasileirão In their final match at MorumBIS in 2026, the Tricolor will host Remo this Thursday (26) at 8 p.m. in the 37th round of the Brazilian Championship. São Paulo sit 11th in the national league, with 45 points from 36 matches. São Paulo have faced the Pará side nine times throughout their history, recording six wins, two draws and one defeat. This will be only the third meeting between the Tricolor and Remo at São Paulo's home ground. São Paulo won the previous two: 2–0 in the 1993 Brazilian Championship and 3–0 in the 1995 Copa do Brasil. Tonight's match will be the Tricolor's 24th and final home game of the season. They have earned 71% of the available points so far, with 15 wins, four draws and four defeats. SÃO PAULO vs REMO This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Mike McCarthy Admits He Said ‘1-2-3 Packers’ vs. Eagles
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy during a game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now PITTSBURGH — Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers went off on head coach Mike McCarthy during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday. Rodgers revealed that McCarthy falls asleep during meetings and snores, and just flat-out misses meetings, too. He thinks McCarthy is unhealthy and his mind is not in the right place. He explained that McCarthy said “1–2-3 Packers” at halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. “We were like what the f*** is going on?” Rodgers said of his teammate’s reactions. “Eight years removed [from Green Bay] and this is a game we need to win.” Rodgers said he genuinely is concerned about McCarthy. “I’m not telling you this to f***ing bury you, but this isn’t healthy and becoming of someone calling the plays,” Rodgers told his longtime head coach. On Wednesday, McCarthy did not comment on the sleeping in meetings part, but he did admit that he said “1–2-3 Packers” at halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy called Rodgers’ 1-2-3 Packers story “embarrassing” and an honest mistake. “The Philadelphia situation at halftime was very emotional. There were conversations prior to that. It was an embarrassing moment, but I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments,” McCarthy said. McCarthy also said he just had a meeting with the team’s leadership council, and believes he has the support of the locker room. “It was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind. … I’m proud of our leadership,” McCarthy said. The Steelers organization is also offering McCarthy “full support” and has no “immediate” plans to fire him, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. “Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, the subject of Aaron Rodgers accusations today, has the full support of the organization, sources say. They are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes,” Rapoport wrote. The Steelers revealed late Tuesday night that they’ve benched Rodgers and that he would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. They are also in the process of releasing the four-time NFL MVP. “There was an ultimatum made that was clearly out of his job description, so I made the decision to bench him,” McCarthy said on Wednesday. Rodgers said he found out he was benched from tight end Pat Freiermuth on a phone call Tuesday night, Freiermuth found out from social media. Rodgers said it was contentious during his last conversation with McCarthy. Rodgers told McCarthy that he thought it was in the best interest of the team for somebody else to call plays and if not, they should release him. Alan Saunders and Brendan Howe provided reporting from Pittsburgh. Related Headlines Steelers Take Rare M

item.title: Now Google’s Familiar Faces AI feature works on Walmart’s $35 smart home camera too
item.description: A couple of Walmart's budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google's familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature. Both cameras and Google's Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera's live video feed.
