item.title: What Happened to Davante Adams, and When Will He Return? Latest on Rams WR’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: What Happened to Davante Adams, and When Will He Return? Latest on Rams WR’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Packers on Thanksgiving Eve Davante Adams isn’t playing in the Los Angeles Rams’ Thanksgiving Eve game against his former team, the Green Bay Packers, on Wednesday night. Asked Friday about a Week 12 return for Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson, head coach Sean McVay admitted: “We’re not quite there yet.” McVay did say there is “a possibility” that Adams plays the following game in Week 13 against the Kansas City Chiefs on Dec. 3. On Monday, two days before kickoff at SoFi Stadium, he backed the receivers who will play in place of Adams and Puka Nacua, whose season is over after surgery. Sean McVay Vouches for the Receivers Filling in for Davante Adams McVay was asked on Monday whether passing on a receiver at the trade deadline was the right decision. “Based on last week, I’m excited about what those guys that did get opportunities did,” he said. “Let’s continue to see if we can grow and figure out what it looks like. You know the information that I had at the time, but I don’t want it to ever be misunderstood. I am confident in Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith and C.J. Daniels [Jr.], and [Brennan] Presley getting a chance to get back there and return kicks. “It’s a bummer to lose those two significant pieces, but I think you have to adjust and adapt. This is the hand that we’re dealt. I’m excited about trying to watch these guys go shine and do everything we can with our decision-making and our thought process to help bring that to life collectively for our group. A lot of that stuff, there have been some moving parts. “The Terrance Ferguson stuff I just found out 30 minutes ago. The Puka [Nacua] stuff was… you gather more information and you decide on getting that surgery. There has been a flexibility that’s been necessary. We’ll look forward to hopefully getting Davante [Adams] back at some point too.” SEE THIS WEEK’S INJURIES: PFN’s NFL Injury Report On Nov. 11, explaining why the Rams didn’t trade for a receiver, McVay said the team was “optimistic” about Adams’ return. In the Rams’ last game, a dominant 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals before their bye week, Mumpfield caught three passes for 81 yards, including a 44-yarder. Smith had two catches, one of them a 22-yard touchdown, and Atwell (31 yards) and Daniels (22) had one catch each. The Rams have won four straight since Adams went down and are 6-4 after a 2-4 start, third in the NFC West. The injury list keeps growing, though. In his opening statement Monday, McVay announced that Ferguson will stay on injured reserve for the rest of the season. Nacua underwent season-ending MCL surgery after going down in Week 9 at the Washington Commanders. item.title: What Happened to Jayden Reed, and When Will He Return? Latest on Packers WR’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Rams on Thanksgiving Eve
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Jayden Reed won’t be on the field tonight when the Green Bay Packers visit the Los Angeles Rams for their Week 12 game at SoFi Stadium. The fourth-year player out of Michigan State suffered a neck injury during the Packers’ Week 2 game against the New York Jets. The Packers subsequently placed Reed on injured reserve, and he will not feature again this season. As of Week 12, Reed has missed 20 regular-season games in four years. How Jayden Reed Got Hurt and Landed on Injured Reserve With a little over 14 minutes left in the opening quarter during the Packers’ Week 2 game against the Jets at MetLife Stadium, Jordan Love called an audible while they were facing second-and-11. The play had them lining up four receivers, two on each side of the offensive line. Reed was lined up at the bottom of the screen, near fellow wideout Matthew Golden, and then ran behind Love and running back Chris Brooks before the ball was snapped. As soon as Love received the ball, he threw a screen pass to Jayden Reed, who was able to get past the line of scrimmage at their 28-yard line. Reed gained four yards before getting tackled by middle linebacker Demario Davis. The collision sent Reed spinning before he went down on the turf. Davis’ teammate, outside linebacker Kingsley Enagbare, also made contact with the defenseless Reed. As the Jets celebrated the stop to bring up third down, Reed was barely moving on the ground. SEE THIS WEEK’S INJURIES: PFN’s NFL Injury Report The Packers’ medical team promptly attended to him as his teammates were nearby to see what was happening. Eventually, Reed was stretchered off the field before play resumed. Despite his absence, the Packers won the game in overtime 20-17. Sports medicine doctor Brian Sutterer explained that when players lower their heads to protect themselves from contact, the natural curve of the cervical spine is lost. Instead, the spine shifts into a straight position, which cannot absorb the impact that comes directly to the crown of the helmet. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed on Sept. 30 that Reed required season-ending neck surgery. Although LaFleur did not believe the injury would end Reed’s career, a definitive timetable for his return in 2027 remains unclear. Reed finished the 2026 season with four receptions for 24 yards. The positive news for Reed, though, is that he and the Packers agreed to a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension. Barring any trade or roster cut, this new deal keeps him on Green Bay’s payroll until the 2029 season. As he recuperates from his neck injury, the Packers have been managing pretty decently without Reed. item.title: Ridley Scott’s Sci-Fi Thriller Masterpiece Is Officially Being Removed From Netflix
item.description: Ridley Scott is one of those staple filmmakers. The 88-year-old English director has made countless noteworthy films, TV shows, and commercials over the course of his prolific career, dabbling in so many genres that it’s difficult to narrow down the parameters of his work. With the release of this year’s The Dog Stars , Scott has directed 31 feature films. They don’t all share the same characteristics, but broadly, his films are known for huge and immersive sets, battles on an epic scale, and big and heady concepts.

item.title: Dayton Flyers head coach, wide receiver earn major PFL awards
item.description: Photo contributed by University of Dayton Football (via Facebook) University of Dayton Football (via Facebook) The Pioneer Football League honored the University of Dayton with several end-of-season honors. [DOWNLOAD: Free WHIO-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Dayton head coach Trevor Andrews was named PFL Coach of the Year, and Gavin Lochow was named Offensive Player of the Year. TRENDING STORIES: Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed due to weather Organizers preparing to feed thousands Thanksgiving dinner in Dayton Woman sentenced in crash that killed 21-year-old Miami County man Lochow became the UD football program’s all-time leader in receptions this season. He passed former Flyer tight end Adam Trautman. Gavin Lochow caught 65 passes for 577 yards and ran 30 times for another 200 yards. He also scored 13 touchdowns (nine receiving, four rushing). Coach Andrews won his first PFL Coach of the Year award. He is the first coach to lead his alma mater to its first PFL title since 2015. Andrews is also a finalist for the Eddie Robinson FCS Coach of the Year Award. Four other Dayton Flyers were named as First Team All-PFL offensive performers: WR Michael Mussari, tight end Donovan Weatherly, offensive lineman (OL) Matthew Barnes, and Zachary McDowell. These Flyers picked up First Team All-PFL defensive honors: DL Mirko Jaksic, LB Joe Kingsbury, and DB Javawn Brooks. Punter Ben Levelle was named to the PFL’s Special Teams First Team. These UD Flyers were named to the Second Team All-PFL team: QB Bryce Schondelmyer, RB Luke Hansen, TE Carson Labensky, and OL Drew Flaherty on offense. DL Collin Ansel, DL Jace Schaefer, LB Sam Schmiesing, and DB Emmanuel Hardrick were each honored on defense. Kicker David Mauer, punt returner Paul Kelly, and long snapper Thomas Tkakady were each named to the PFL’s Special Teams Second Team. RB Mason Hackett and kickoff returner LeRoy Lewis IV each earned PFL honorable mention nods. Dayton plays at Tennessee Tech in the first round of the 2026 FCS Playoffs on Saturday, Nov. 28. Kickoff is at 2 p.m. in Cookeville, Tennessee. Larry Hansgen and Mike Kelly broadcast the game on WHIO Radio . [SIGN UP: WHIO-TV Daily Headlines Newsletter ]

item.title: Patriots Insider Reveals Why Team Doesn't Want Daniel Jones
item.description: Patriots Insider Reveals Why Team Doesn't Want Daniel Jones originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the Patriots ' season hangs by a thread, many have started to believe the team could find a proven quarterback to save it as Drake Maye continues to recover from his injury. With Daniel Jones available, as the Indianapolis Colts released him and he cleared waivers, he was instantly viewed as a potential option in New England. However, head coach Mike Vrabel made it clear Monday morning that he has no plans to bring in another quarterback. That may change depending on how things go for Tommy DeVito and the Patriots' offense against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday afternoon in Los Angeles. However, the latest reasoning for Jones not being on the Patriots' radar makes some sense. While he's undoubtedly a better player than DeVito at this stage of his career, a Patriots beat reporter for The Athletic suggested that New England doesn't want to bring in Jones to learn this offense and hope everything will go as planned. “For starters, even if Jones is probably slightly better than DeVito, the team doesn’t seem to feel like the gap between them is so wide that it’s worth putting Jones through a crash course on an offense DeVito already understands well. The coaching staff has worked with DeVito for a year. The staff appreciates his work ethic and has been impressed by some throws in preseason games. “Now, the Patriots want to roll with the backup-level quarterback they know — and, crucially, the one who knows their system — over the one they don’t,” Chad Graff of The Athletic wrote . Because DeVito already understands this offense, it's not wrong to think that Vrabel and the Patriots are making the right decision here. The problem with DeVito is that he hasn't really proven much throughout his career, playing in just 15 games and throwing for nine touchdowns and four interceptions. He had a nice little run with the New York Giants in 2023, but he hasn't done much since. In a way, the same can be said about Jones, but he has much more experience and has, frankly, proven more at this point. item.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
item.description: Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland ruled in favor of the CPSC, which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods , not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products. Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025 after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 "Fulfilled by Amazon" products that pose a "substantial product hazard," including faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers without electrocution protection, and child … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Awka City chosen for AfDB -funded Action Plan for Africa’s coordinated urban development
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Awka, the capital city of Anambra State, has been selected for the African Development Bank, AfDB, – funded action plan for coordinated urban development in Africa. Under the programme, government would provide the policy direction, regulatory clarity, and institutional leadership, while development partners would support the mobilisation of technical expertise and catalytic resources. Also, the private sector is expected to play a decisive role in financing and delivering viable infrastructure and urban projects, traditional institutions, community leaders, professional bodies and residents will remain vital in safeguarding public ownership and ensuring that development stays centred on the people in the new city. At the launch of the plan on Wednesday in Awka, the state governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo said it is part of the strategic plan to create the envisioned Anambra mega city. Represented by his special Adviser on trade and commerce, Mr. Christian Udechukwu, the governor recalled that Awka is the only city chosen in Africa for the project, noting that it is because of the long term vision and the strategic implementation and the intentionality and purposeful focus of the administration. According to Udechukwu, it is the governor’s determination to transform Anambra State that drew the attention of the African Development Bank to the state. “The reforms they see here are of significance that it would serve to use Awka City as a model to prove the sustainability of the project and we are happy that this is happening under this administration”, he said. He said that a substantial amount of next year’s budget would be devoted to the development of the new Awka City, while other cities of Onitsha, Nnewi, and Ekwulobia would also undergo transformation, in addition to the new cities planned for the state. “When Awka 2.0 joins the planned industrial city, the proposed axis of prosperity would have been created. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Vincent Ujumadu Awka, the capital city of Anambra State, has been selected for the African Development Bank, AfDB, – funded action plan for coordinated urban development in Africa. Under the programme, government would provide the policy direction, regulatory clarity, and institutional leadership, while development partners would support the mobilisation of technical expertise and catalytic resources. Also, the private sector is expected to play a decisive role in financing and delivering viable infrastructure and urban projects, traditional institutions, community leaders, professional bodies and residents will remain vital in safeguarding public ownership and ensuring that development stays centred on the people in the new city. At the launch of the plan on Wednesday in Awka, the state governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo said it is part of the strategic plan to create the envisioned Anambra mega city. Represented by his special Adviser on trade and commerce, Mr. Christian Udechukwu, the governor recalled that Awka is the only city chosen in Africa for the project, noting that it is because of the long term vision and the strategic implementation and the intentionality and purposeful focus of the administration. According to Udechukwu, it is the governor’s determination to transform Anambra State that drew the attention of the African Development Bank to the state. “The reforms they see here are of significance that it would serve to use Awka City as a model to prove the sustainability of the project and we are happy that this is happening under this administration”, he said. He said that a substantial amount of next year’s budget would be devoted to the development of the new Awka City, while other cities of Onitsha, Nnewi, and Ekwulobia would also undergo transformation, in addition to the new cities planned for the state. “When Awka 2.0 joins the planned industrial city, the proposed axis of prosperity would have been created. So Anambra is being positioned to become the economic hub of Nigeria and that is why the selection of Awka as a primary model sustainable city in Africa is important to us as a government. We should therefore not waste more time to move into the project preparatory stage”, Udechukwu said. Speaking at the launch, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Awka Capital Territory Development Authority, ACTDA, Dr Osita Onuko said the coordinated development framework is aimed at addressing the growing infrastructure and environmental challenges confronting Awka and guiding the capital city’s expansion towards a more liveable and inclusive future. The ACTDA boss said the action plan should be viewed not merely as a technical document, but as a shared commitment to building a productive, resilient and inclusive capital city for future generations He said: “This ambition aligns directly with the vision of His Excellency, Governor Chukwuma Soludo, to transform Anambra into a liveable and prosperous smart megacity by 2050. Achieving that vision requires clear urban direction, sustained investment, and strong institutions capable of translating bold aspirations into tangible outcomes. “Like many rapidly growing African cities, Awka is experiencing mounting pressure on its urban infrastructure, public services, and environment. The steady expansion of our built environment, rising demand for housing and utilities, traffic congestion, flooding, and gully erosion all highlight the urgent need for a more integrated approach to urban management. “These challenges are deeply interconnected. Addressing them effectively means that decisions around land use, mobility, housing, utilities, environmental protection, and economic development must be considered together within one coherent framework. Without this alignment, interventions risk becoming fragmented, resources are inefficiently deployed, and opportunities for lasting impact are lost. “The Awka City Action Plan provides that common framework. It establishes a shared direction for our capital’s growth, identifies clear priority areas for intervention, and creates a practical structure to align government spending, private sector investment, and development partner support. “With the document now complete, our immediate focus turns to translating these priorities into bankable, well-prepared projects that can attract financing and deliver lasting value. For ACTDA, this means providing strong institutional leadership and coordination—working hand-in-hand with relevant ministries, departments, and agencies to ensure this plan actively guides our regulatory decisions and investment discussions. We are committed to accountability, continuity, and measurable results so that this becomes a living framework rather than a document left on a shelf.” The post Awka City chosen for AfDB -funded Action Plan for Africa’s coordinated urban development appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How to get adrenaline in GTA 6
item.description: Adrenaline acts as an emergency boost to all your stats in Grand Theft Auto 6 , as it temporarily negates health, stamina, and focus loss. It's meant to get you out of an emergency situation safely or help you burst into a tense situation and mop it up fast. Unlike Zombix and other restoratives, though, you can't buy adrenaline — not from anywhere we've found so far, at least — nor can you expect to find it in abundance throughout Leonida. There is, however, a small set of locations you can reliably get adrenaline from.

item.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
item.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. "We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess," said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. "H owever, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle." Artist's illustration of the Hera spacecraft with its two deployable CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in the vicinity of the Didymos binary asteroid system. Credit: ESA-Science Office Following up The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera's first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across. Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there's no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren't sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth. " I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid," said Patrick Michel, Hera's principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. "In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen." item.dc:creator: Stephen Clark
item.content:encoded: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. "We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess," said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. "H owever, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle." Artist's illustration of the Hera spacecraft with its two deployable CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in the vicinity of the Didymos binary asteroid system. Credit: ESA-Science Office Following up The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera's first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across. Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there's no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren't sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth. " I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid," said Patrick Michel, Hera's principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. "In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen." Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable. "As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” says Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist. The Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid's composition, internal structure, and mass. Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART's impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos's physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids. "Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense," Michel said in an interview with Ars. This is a composite image combining 11 long-exposure images from Hera's Hyperscout-H instrument, centered on the Didymos asteroid. The dot trails correspond to hundreds of boulders of differing sizes in motion around the Didymos-Dimorphos system. The two asteroids have been subtracted from the image for improved visualization of the boulders. These images were acquired on November 6 with an approximate distance of 29.9 kilometers (18.6 miles) from the asteroids. What a mess In its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART's impact showed a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos , but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera's first images. "As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we quickly realized the asteroids were not alone," said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l'Aéronautique et de l'Espace in Toulouse, France. "In fact, they had a lot of company." Read full article Comments

item.title: Malen penalty ends PSG’s perfect UCL run as Roma snatch 2-2 draw
item.description: Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end. Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out. Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own. The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team. They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches. It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the play-off round like in the last two campaigns. But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness too and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result. Dembele’s presence on the bench at kick-off meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season were in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos. Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend. – Dembele spot-kick – However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital. They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert. Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time. Evan Ndicka headed just off-target for Roma late in the first half and Niccolo Pisilli forced a good stop from Matvei Safonov early in the second half. Joao Neves then headed agonisingly wide for PSG as he arrived unmarked in the area to meet a Nuno Mendes cross, before Dembele was introduced for the hosts in place of the ineffective Ferran Torres. Moments after that PSG won a penalty when Achraf Hakimi stormed into the Roma box only to be pulled down by Wesley. The French side had missed four penalties in the Champions League since the start of last season, but Dembele did score in the final against Arsenal in May. He kept a cool head to convert his fifth goal of the campaign, but PSG could not make it five straight Champions League wins this season. Malen entered the fray for Roma midway through the second half and looked on as Dembele was denied a brilliant solo goal by a Mile Svilar save. Roma then won a penalty following a VAR check after Vitinha blocked a Soule shot with a raised hand in the box. Up stepped Malen to score his 17th goal of a prolific campaign, boosting Roma’s hopes of reaching the knockout phase. item.title: Le Pen party leaks: prefect dismissed, Paris deputy prosecutor placed under investigation
item.description: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right party of Marine Le Pen, the National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret, Hugues Moutouh, a former top official at the Interior Ministry, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. And a deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now under administrative inquiry. FRANCE 24's Camille Knight reports.

item.title: Capcom Is Officially Killing Its 'Jurassic World Meets Overwatch' Shooter
item.description: Four years after the game's launch , Capcom is officially shutting down Exoprimal , the company's 5v5 action game about a futuristic dinosaur crisis. Capcom announced Tuesday that service for Exoprimal will be discontinued in September 2027 — meaning that Exoprimal will no longer be playable — and that the game will no longer be sold starting in March 2027.

item.title: UCL: Pochettino still winless as Man United draw 2-2 with Sporting
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side. United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half. Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game. United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match. item.dc:creator: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
item.content:encoded: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side. United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half. Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game. United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match. A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick. Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha. Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control. Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty. The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later. Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot. – United unhappy with disallowed goals – United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay. Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded. Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez. The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner. Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season. The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch. Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head. The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick. Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting battled to find an equaliser. It eventually came from a howler from Lammens, who failed to claim a cross dropping out of the sky, spilling the ball in front of Suarez, who produced a hooked acrobatic effort to score. Moments later United had the ball in the net at the other end after another goalkeeping error by Pereira, who mishandled Fernandes’s corner, pushing the ball into his own net. However what would have been the winner was disallowed for an elbow by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper, a decision the visitors were also unhappy about. item.title: Dangote Refinery to list on Nigerian Exchange December 1
item.description: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery says it will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) Group on December 1, marking its entry into the Nigerian stock market following its initial public offering (IPO). Devakumar Edwin, vice-president of oil and gas at Dangote Group, announced the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s share allocation plan following its heavily oversubscribed IPO, which closed last month. The regulatory approval cleared the way for the company to distribute shares to investors and proceed with preparations for its stock market debut. The refinery had earlier sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong investor demand. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), said the refinery planned to pursue a listing on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, Africa’s richest person said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and globally. Vanguard News The post Dangote Refinery to list on Nigerian Exchange December 1 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: New US tariffs: 'Trump lashing out really indiscriminately', expert says
item.description: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Dean Baker, Senior Economist at the Centre for Economic and Policy Research, says that "there has to be some mechanism for better coordinating China's involvement in the world trade system and ideally the US, the EU, Canada would have a common front, some clear ground rules that we could agree to, that China could agree to, to be mutually beneficial. It's not a step in that direction, we have President Trump lashing out really indiscriminately. It's very hard to see his approach being very productive".

item.title: Lammens errors cost Manchester United victory in frantic finale at Sporting
item.description: “We are a strong team,” Mauricio Pochettino exhorted, then watched Manchester United’s unerring ability to cause drama every time they lace up their boots. Cruising, it seemed, at 2-1 and with 10 minutes left, they unravelled, as Senne Lammens dropped a high ball in front of his goal and a grateful Luis Suárez equalised with a bicycle kick. Cut almost instantly to Sporting’s Kaique Pereira who bundled the ball in for United’s apparent winner only for Szymon Marciniak to be ordered to the screen by the video assistant referee, where the official ruled the goal out for a foul on the goalkeeper by Patrick Dorgu. item.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
item.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees. item.content:encoded: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. The table below details moonrise timings for a selection of cities spread across the globe for Dec. 23-24: Local moonrise timings for the December 2026 full Cold Moon City Local time New York 3:58 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 London 4:07 p.m. GMT on Dec. 24 Tokyo 4:32 p.m. JST on Dec. 24 Beijing 4:55 p.m. CST on Dec. 24 Sydney 8:36 p.m. AEDT on Dec. 24 Why it's called the Cold Moon The December full moon is often called the Cold Moon in reference to the often freezing temperatures that can descend this time of the year. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees. The December full moon also coincides with the Hindu festival of Datta Jayanti, when followers gather to celebrate the birth of Lord Dattatreya, who embodies the Hindu holy trinity of Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, according to the Government of Maharashtra . The December full moon also rises close to the Christian celebration of Christmas on Dec. 25, when followers celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ. What else to see in the sky around the full moon The Cold Moon will shine in the center of a majestic "Winter Hexagon" of stars bright enough to easily cut through the glare cast by the lunar disk after it rises on Nov. 24. Begin by locating Sirius, the brightest star in our night sky, which rises into the southeastern sky shortly after 8 p.m. local time for viewers in New York. Next, trace an imaginary line to the blue supergiant star Rigel in the nearby constellation Orion, before hopping to the orange glow of Aldebaran , which represents an eye of the great bull depicted in the constellation Taurus. Looking south at midnight on Dec. 23-24 (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva with assets from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio) Next we move to Capella, the jewel of the constellation Auriga, before jumping down to Pollux in the constellation Gemini and nearby Procyon, before closing the loop with Sirius once more. Jupiter and the red light of Mars will shine low in the eastern sky in the hour before midnight, while Saturn will lurk close to the western horizon. Look to the southeast just before dawn to spot Venus appearing as a brilliant "Morning Star", with the red giant Arcturus shining higher in the predawn sky close to the constellation Bootes. Observing tips The December full moon presents a stunning opportunity to photograph the lunar disk as it shines in Earth's sky entirely free from shadow. Be sure to make use of our expert guide to photographing the moon , along with our picks of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography , if you want to upgrade your equipment. Observing tips Use a tripod to keep your camera as steady as possible. Use a remote shutter release or self-timer to prevent camera wobble. A smartphone stargazing app can help you find the exact point of moonrise on your local horizon. A 12–50 mm lens is useful for landscape photography, while at least 400 mm is advised for capturing more detailed views of the lunar surface. The moon can be made to appear particularly large while close to the horizon next to foreground objects, where it may take on an orange-yellow appearance thanks to Rayleigh scattering. A cleaner, more "classic" view can be captured as it soars high overhead. Upcoming full moons Month Full moon name Date and time January Wolf Moon 7:17 a.m. EST (1217 GMT) on Jan. 22, 2027 February Snow Moon 6:23 p.m. EST (2323 GMT) on Feb. 20, 2027 March Worm Moon 6:43 a.m. EST (1043 GMT) on March 22, 2027 These times mark the exact instant of full illumination. Your own moonrise or moonset may be hours earlier or later, depending on your location. For the best viewing plan, use an app such as Stellarium or SkySafari 7 Pro . Editor's Note: If you would like to share your full moon photos with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s) along with your name, the location and any comments on what it was like to capture the picture to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in furtherance of ongoing counter-terrorism operations, on Wednesday successfully rescued 5 kidnapped victims and arrested of 2 suspected terrorists in separate operations conducted in Kaduna State. Confirming the rescue operation, Captain Sinivie Tamuno, Spokesman said, “On Wednesday, 25 November 2026, troops of Sector 1 responded to distress calls following attacks by suspected terrorists on Dan Bushiya community in Chikun Local Government Area, during which some residents were abducted. “Despite encountering an ambush, troops continued their rescue efforts without sustaining any casualties. “The operation led to the rescue of a woman and her baby, who were abandoned by the fleeing terrorists following sustained pressure from the troops. “Similarly, on the same day, troops responded to another distress call following the abduction of 5 residents of Kakura village in the same Local Government Area. “The swift intervention of the troops forced the terrorists to abandon 3 of the kidnapped victims, who were subsequently rescued. “Efforts are ongoing in conjunction with other security agencies to track and eliminate the terrorists. “In a related development, on the same day, a joint patrol team conducting search and rescue operations following a kidnapped incident in Danbushiya community, found a national ID card along the terrorists’ withdraw route. “The discovery subsequently led to the arrest of the bearer identified as Mr Shauibu Musa and another suspect named Aliyu Ahmed. “The suspected terrorists are in troops custody for further investigation. The Joint Task Force Operation Fansan Yamma remains resolute in its commitment to combating terrorism and other forms of criminality, securing lives and property, and restoring lasting peace across the North West. “Members of the public are urged to continue supporting ongoing operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious activities to the troops and other security agencies.” The post Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
item.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. He also called on countries yet to ratify the treaty, particularly African nations, to do so, pledging Nigeria’s commitment to working wi

The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
item.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: [VIDEO] 2027: Tinubu Will Have A Big Battle In His Hands If Election Goes Into A Runoff — Simon Kolawole
item.description: Publisher of TheCable, Simon Kolawole, has said that President Bola Tinubu will face a tough task if the 2027 presidential election does not end on the first ballot. Kolawole stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that the opposition parties would come together to form an alliance to defeat the incumbent president if the January 16, 2027, election enters a runoff. The publisher and author said the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, controls the South-East and is expected to win in the five states that make up the region. He, however, said that while Obi won in the South-East region, he got only 20 per cent in the South-West and six per cent in the core North, a performance he said has to improve in the 2027 election. Watch the full interview in the video below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] 2027: Tinubu Will Have A Big Battle In His Hands If Election Goes Into A Runoff — Simon Kolawole appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: “I Don Finally Make My Mama Proud”: Asisat Oshoala Graduates With a Master’s Degree
item.description: Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala in her graduation gown and cap at Wembley Stadium after earning her MSc in International Sports Management. Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala has added a brand-new title to her name—and this time, it comes with a graduation cap and gown. The Nigerian football star graduated today, Wednesday, 25 November 2026, with a Master of Science (MSc) degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sport (GIS) at a ceremony held at Wembley Stadium in London. Sharing photos from the graduation on her Instagram Story, the forward kept her caption short, sweet, and full of charm: “I don finally make my mama proud.” Long before collecting European trophies and continental awards, the Ikorodu-born athlete attended Aunty Ayo International School in Lagos, where she first started playing football before pursuing the sport professionally. Now, alongside her playing career, she holds a postgraduate master’s degree in sports management—equipping herself for leadership roles off the pitch as well as on it. Asisat Oshoala holds two bouquets of flowers while celebrating her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium. On the field, Oshoala remains one of Africa’s most decorated footballers. Playing primarily as a centre-forward—and occasionally out wide as a winger—the 32-year-old represents Nigeria on the international stage as a key pillar of the Super Falcons, and currently plays club football in the Saudi Women’s Premier League for Al-Hilal, following spells with Arsenal, Liverpool, Dalian Quanjian, FC Barcelona Femení, and Bay FC. Her footballing CV speaks for itself. A six-time CAF African Women’s Footballer of the Year—the first player in history to win the honour six times—Oshoala has won multiple UEFA Women’s Champions League trophies with Barcelona, claimed Liga F and Women’s Super League titles, and represented Nigeria across multiple FIFA Women’s World Cups and Olympic Games. Beyond football, she also runs the Asisat Oshoala Academy and Foundation, which empowers young girls in Nigeria through sports and education. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium alongside her mother and loved ones. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Master of Science degree in International Sports Management at Wembley Stadium. The post “I Don Finally Make My Mama Proud”: Asisat Oshoala Graduates With a Master’s Degree appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
item.description: Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control. Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year. The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules. Read full article Comments

Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control. Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year. The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules. Read full article Comments

item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: APC’s Strategy Is To Ensure NDC Candidates Can’t Campaign Nationwide — Olumide Akpata
item.description: A former president of the Nigerian Bar Association, Olumide Akpata, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of plotting to frustrate candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and prevent them from campaigning across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. Akpata, who is a chieftain of the NDC, spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today while reacting to the attack on members of the party by armed hoodlums in Benin City, ahead of the visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to Edo State, on Wednesday. He decried the intimidation and hostility shown by the APC against the NDC, saying that two facility owners the opposition party had paid to have their town hall meeting in Benin City refunded the payment when they received calls not to allow the event to hold there. Akpata, who contested the Edo State governorship election in 2024, also recalled how hoodlums invaded his office in the state capital and opened fire. He called on the ruling APC to allow Nigerian voters to decide whether they have done well, rather than resort to violence. While responding to a question about the rig-and-die slogan attributed to the NDC, Akpata said anybody caught rigging should face the full wrath of the law. The former NBA president said that the NDC will not back down in the face of intimidation. He also said that the opposition party would ensure that the matter is not swept under the carpet. “We are not going to sink to the despicable depths these other persons are willing to do,” he added. Watch the full interview below. ﻿ The post [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: APC’s Strategy Is To Ensure NDC Candidates Can’t Campaign Nationwide — Olumide Akpata appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‘Five bullets’ — NDC supporter recounts attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta
item.description: A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has recounted how gunmen allegedly shot him five times during an attack on the campaign team of Ovie Omo-Agege, the party’s candidate for Delta Central, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The survivor, who sustained gunshot injuries to his chest and mouth, narrated his ordeal in a video shared on the NDC’s X page on Wednesday. The video showed him speaking from his hospital bed during a visit by Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, its vice-presidential candidate, to survivors of the attack. Recounting events leading up to the shooting, the man said he had received threats after participating in a 10,000-man march organised by the NDC in Delta State. According to him, his wife received a telephone call from individuals who threatened to shut down his business. “To be very precise, on Sunday, when we were in church, in the early hours of the day, they went and sealed the whole business premises. I could not get access to the premises; I could not offload my goods,” he recalled. “A week later, my truck that brought goods from Lagos, they seized the truck and drove it to the local government secretariat.” He said the truck was detained for more than four days, adding that no explanation had been provided for its seizure. The supporter said the attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters at the campaign venue, when gunmen stormed the gathering and opened fire. He said one of the attackers called out his name before shooting him as he attempted to escape towards his car. “One of them started shouting, ‘That is Agba, shoot Agba, that is Agba, look at Agba going.’ Before I could say Jack, the gunshot came straight to my chest,” he said. “There is a bullet here, through the throat. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth. “So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.” He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates. “The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said. Another survivor receiving treatment at the hospital also expressed determination to continue supporting the party despite the violence. “No matter the number of persons they shoot or attempt to kill in their time, Peter Obi will become president, Rabiu Kwankwaso will become vice-president, and Nigeria will be okay,” he said. Recall in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Nigeria Police Force spokesperson, Ani Iniedu, said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed and several others injured during the attack. Iniedu said the police would sanction any officers found to have acted improperly, unlawfully or breached professional standards during the incident. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth. “So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.” He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates. “The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said. item.title: Did GTA 6 really recreate Charlie Kirk's assassination?
item.description: Just days after its release, Grand Theft Auto 6 has become a vehicle for political misinformation. Viral footage falsely claims the game features a mission recreating Charlie Kirk’s assassination, while pro-Russian accounts are sharing fake screenshots containing anti-Ukrainian messages. Meanwhile, Russia’s own Defence Ministry has exploited the game's popularity to promote military recruitment. item.title: Davido, Patoranking, Cubana Chief Priest to attend Odii’s Ebonyi gov’ship campaign flag-off
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Popular Nigerian music artists, Davido and Patoranking, as well as celebrity businessman and socialite Cubana Chief Priest, will storm, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State capital Thursday for the official flag-off of the governorship campaign of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii. Other people expected at the event are international businessmen, politicial bigwigs and over 300 friends of Odii across Nigeria and beyond to support their own to actualize his dream of becoming the next governor come 2027. Odii who stated in a media roundtable pledged that his administration, if elected, will not abandon ongoing or uncompleted projects across the state, promising to prioritise continuity, accountability and proper execution of development projects. He said his campaign would be issue-based, reaffirmed his determination to pursue sustainable economic development. He explained that his administration would be guided by a comprehensive manifesto designed to address Ebonyi State’s present realities, past challenges and future development aspirations. According to him, the manifesto would serve as a roadmap for governance, clearly outlining the promises and programmes his administration intends to implement from the beginning of its tenure. The PDP governorship candidate maintained that governance should not be about making unrealistic political promises but about identifying existing projects, assessing their relevance and ensuring that viable investments are completed and put to productive use. “We will never abandon any project. If we must do it, we will have to do it properly,” he declared. Odii further promised to conduct a comprehensive assessment of ongoing and abandoned projects across the state to determine the resources and interventions required to complete them. He also stressed the importance of strengthening the state’s economy, noting that a stronger economic base would improve the government’s capacity to deliver infrastructure and other development commitments. On the issue of political violence, intimidation and thuggery, Odii condemned all forms of electoral violence, assuring supporters that his political ambition was driven by a genuine desire to bring about a change in governance. He expressed confidence that intimidation and other political attacks would not derail his ambition. “We mean business. We are not joking. We are fighting for a change in government. We know it, but by the grace of God, nothing can stop us,” he said. Odii, in turn, expressed his campaign’s readiness to strengthen its media engagement and public communication strategy to reach more residents across the rural and urban areas of the state. The PDP guber candidate later inaugurated his campaign council led Ambassador Nwanne Ominyi as Director General where he charged them to based their campaign on Issue-based not name calling or character assisination. He also charged them to shun violence, thuggery or to reply

item.title: Which gaming headsets are worth the cost? I put 20 to the test – here are the best for 2026
item.description: Wired, wireless, noise cancelling and budget … here are the headphones to level up your PC and console gaming • The best gaming chairs We talk a lot about graphics in video games; we know how important it is to play on a decent screen so we can see what we’re shooting at … or running away from. But what about sound? Explosions, dialogue, the wheezy breathing of a nearby monster – arguably, audio quality is just as important. Many modern games now support 3D or spatial audio, which lets you detect exactly where a sound is coming from in the game world. In survival horror adventures, you can hear the zombie lurking in the next room, and in popular shooters such as Fortnite and Apex Legends, you can pinpoint the footsteps of approaching enemies. item.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. Vanguard News The post 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Campaign rules for influencers? French regulator targets content creators
item.description: Ever since 1965 when the French first got to cast a ballot by universal suffrage for their president, they've valued campaign rules that guarantee ‘equal time’ for candidates. But what does equal time mean when you're closing in on 2027? Last week a bombshell announcement ahead of next Spring’s presidential elections: major online content creators will have to respect the same balanced air time rules as traditional TV and radio broadcasters during the campaign period. Here at France 24, we’re already testing the stopwatches and combing ove the guest list spreadsheets. Should podcasters, YouTubers and influencers be subjected to the same rules as us?

item.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
item.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. Vanguard News The post Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EU says 'strongly' rejects premise of new US tariffs
item.description: The EU said Wednesday that it rejected the premise of new tariffs on its exports proposed by the United States and expected Washington to stick by a deal struck with Brussels last year. The US unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production. FRANCE 24's Dave Keating reports from Brussels.
