item.dc:creator: Lindsay Clark
item.content:encoded: Microsoft has brought its HorizonDB PostgreSQL service into public preview in Fabric, aiming to bring transactional and analytical workloads closer together. The corporation says applications can submit queries through a single PostgreSQL endpoint, with transactional and analytical work handled by the appropriate engines. Analysts said the move follows similar efforts by Databricks and Snowflake to combine operational databases with analytics. But tighter integration with Microsoft's stack could make applications harder to move elsewhere. Fabric HorizonDB joins SQL database and Cosmos DB in Microsoft's Fabric database portfolio. "By bringing operational databases, analytics, and AI together on a unified, governed platform, developers can build intelligent applications with less data movement and complexity. Fabric HorizonDB will also serve as the PostgreSQL backend for Fabric apps," Microsoft said. Microsoft first unveiled Azure HorizonDB in preview in November 2025 and made it generally available last week. It competes with other cloud database services and distributed systems such as CockroachDB and YugabyteDB, both of which support PostgreSQL's wire protocol. At the time, it said HorizonDB would offer "massive read scale without the need to replicate the database between instances." Speaking to The Register last week, Shireesh Thota, veep of Azure databases and Fabric applications, said that bringing the system into Fabric – its platform for data lakes, data warehouses, and analytics launched in 2023 – would connect operational data in HorizonDB with analytical data in OneLake, Fabric's unified data lake. "Once the data hits the OneLake storage, you can have analytical engines that take advantage of it. In HorizonDB, the PostgreSQL query engine can talk to the distributed query engine that we use in our Fabric data warehouse. We're fusing these query engines, thereby enabling the developers to submit a query that has pieces of the query that can work on OLTP and pieces of the query that can work on OLAP," he said. "The application need not worry about two endpoints, or about consistency of data and all that complexity. They can just talk to HorizonDB as a Fabric endpoint, and they can submit all these queries. We are basically operationalizing in OneLake." Operational data remains in HorizonDB's database storage, while mirroring maintains an analytical copy in OneLake, introduced in 2023 , which replicates a snapshot of the external database to OneLake in Delta Parquet tables and keeps the replica synced in "near real time." Thota said the process would not affect the transactional system. "Our core goal is to never impact OLTP workload while we are doing this, and we succeed [by] reading off the log as an additional replica to do this mirroring," he said. But the overall plan of putting serverless PostgreSQL OLTP in an analytics platform, bringing it close to OLAP systems, is one some vendors are already executing to meet the demands of new AI agent-led workloads. Adam Ronthal, research veep in Gartner's Data and Analytics Group, said: "The addition of Microsoft Fabric HorizonDB follows the 2025 acquisitions of PostgreSQL vendors by Databricks – Neon – and Snowflake – Crunchy. It delivers a high-performance, serverless operational RDBMS that is tightly coupled with Microsoft's lakehouse offering and well-suited to the ephemeral demands of AI agents. "Competing directly with AWS Aurora and Google Cloud's AlloyDB, HorizonDB acts as a foundational serving layer for the next generation of AI- and analytics-infused applications. For organizations aligned with Azure and Fabric, it provides an industry-standard PostgreSQL foundation for AI development." Andrew Snodgrass, research vice president of analyst company Directions on Microsoft, said the announcement of HorizonDB in Fabric was a "surprise," although "a watered-down version" compared to the version of the serverless database that became generally available on Azure last week. "It joins (document database) CosmosDB in Fabric and SQL database (based on the SQL Server engine) in Fabric. It highlights that Microsoft is still focused on making Fabric the data hub of their universe." HorizonDB – both in Azure and Fabric – is a PostgreSQL service which Microsoft says has 100 percent compatibility with the open source system that has enjoyed a meteoric rise over the last decade. The support for PostgreSQL has led some to question the software giant's commitment to its own proprietary OLTP system, SQL Server. Thota pointed out that the SQL database , based on the SQL Server engine, is already available in Fabric. Microsoft is also evaluating similar integration for that service, although he gave no timetable. "We are just beginning this journey, and most of the innovation is neutral to PostgreSQL and SQL. Some of it would be particular to how the individual query engine fuses with the analytical query engine. PostgreSQL does it slightly differently than SQL, but the idea is that most of the work is neutral. We are evaluating that work as well. I don't have timelines for that, but it is certainly in our thinking," he said. Nonetheless, Holger Mueller, principal analyst at Constellation Research, said it was good to see Microsoft go all in on support of open source. "In general, it is an acknowledgement that they cannot win the battle for the SQL database with SQL Server – as it is as proprietary as the leader Oracle – and now they bank on the openness of PostgreSQL as another approach," he said. However, using HorizonDB integrated into the Fabric/Azure stack may create so many dependencies with Microsoft's technology that lock-in to the vendor will remain a risk. "The primary concerns of open source – scale and support – have been eliminated by Microsoft's commitment and by now track record... the challenges are the embeddings of HorizonDB into the bigger Microsoft stack – which will make portability hard again. But every vendor wants and provides stickiness – clothed in ease of use and lower TCO," Mueller said. ®

item.title: Senegal Reinstated as 2025 AFCON Champions After Winning CAS Appeal
item.description: Idrissa Gana Gueye and captain Sadio Mané hold the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations trophy, which the Court of Arbitration for Sport confirmed belongs to Senegal after setting aside CAF’s Appeal Board decision. The months-long off-pitch dispute surrounding the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final has come to an official close, with Senegal reinstated as the tournament’s champions. Today, Tuesday, 24 November 2026, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) —the independent international body headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, that settles global sports disputes through arbitration—ruled unanimously in favour of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) . The verdict overturns the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board’s earlier decision that stripped the Teranga Lions of the trophy and handed a 3–0 forfeit victory to hosts Morocco. For football lovers across the continent, many of whom watched two of Africa’s finest sides battle through one of the most dramatic finals in AFCON history, the verdict restores the outcome decided on the pitch in Rabat on 18 January 2026. In that January final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Senegal edged Morocco 1–0 after extra time courtesy of a decisive strike from Pape Gueye . However, the match had been halted late in regulation time while still goalless after referee Jean – Jacques Ngambo Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review. Several Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest for roughly 14 minutes before returning—following interventions from teammates including captain Sadio Mané —to finish the match in the 109th minute (90+19). Morocco’s Brahim Díaz missed the resulting penalty, and Senegal went on to win in extra time. Senegal celebrate their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations triumph in Rabat—a title officially restored on 24 November 2026 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned CAF’s forfeiture ruling. Two months later, in March 2026, CAF’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal’s temporary walk-off amounted to a forfeiture under Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, awarding Morocco a 3–0 administrative win and the championship. The FSF lodged its appeal with CAS on 25 March 2026, followed by a closed-door hearing in Lausanne on 8 October 2026 before a three-member panel presided over by French sports law expert Prof. Gérald Simon , alongside Prof. Luigi Fumagalli (Italy) and Prof. Dr. Ulrich Haas (Germany). In its official statement released today, CAS confirmed that Senegal’s original victory stands: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Idrissa Gana Gueye and captain Sadio Mané hold the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations trophy, which the Court of Arbitration for Sport confirmed belongs to Senegal after setting aside CAF’s Appeal Board decision. The months-long off-pitch dispute surrounding the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) final has come to an official close, with Senegal reinstated as the tournament’s champions. Today, Tuesday, 24 November 2026, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) —the independent international body headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, that settles global sports disputes through arbitration—ruled unanimously in favour of the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) . The verdict overturns the Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board’s earlier decision that stripped the Teranga Lions of the trophy and handed a 3–0 forfeit victory to hosts Morocco. For football lovers across the continent, many of whom watched two of Africa’s finest sides battle through one of the most dramatic finals in AFCON history, the verdict restores the outcome decided on the pitch in Rabat on 18 January 2026. In that January final at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium, Senegal edged Morocco 1–0 after extra time courtesy of a decisive strike from Pape Gueye . However, the match had been halted late in regulation time while still goalless after referee Jean – Jacques Ngambo Ndala awarded Morocco a penalty following a VAR review. Several Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest for roughly 14 minutes before returning—following interventions from teammates including captain Sadio Mané —to finish the match in the 109th minute (90+19). Morocco’s Brahim Díaz missed the resulting penalty, and Senegal went on to win in extra time. Senegal celebrate their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations triumph in Rabat—a title officially restored on 24 November 2026 after the Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned CAF’s forfeiture ruling. Two months later, in March 2026, CAF’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal’s temporary walk-off amounted to a forfeiture under Articles 82 and 84 of the competition regulations, awarding Morocco a 3–0 administrative win and the championship. The FSF lodged its appeal with CAS on 25 March 2026, followed by a closed-door hearing in Lausanne on 8 October 2026 before a three-member panel presided over by French sports law expert Prof. Gérald Simon , alongside Prof. Luigi Fumagalli (Italy) and Prof. Dr. Ulrich Haas (Germany). In its official statement released today, CAS confirmed that Senegal’s original victory stands: “The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025). The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 fo r Senegal).” Explaining its reasoning, the panel noted that the referee’s decision to restart play fell squarely within his sole authority and was protected by football’s “field of play” doctrine, meaning it could not be overturned retrospectively. “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume,” CAS stated. “In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the ‘field of play’ doctrine.” Senegal captain Sadio Mané celebrates on his teammates’ shoulders with the 2025 AFCON trophy, officially restored to the Teranga Lions after CAS ruled in favour of the Senegalese Football Federation. The panel also rejected arguments from the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) that the referee had acted arbitrarily or erred in law, adding that Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations apply only when a match is permanently abandoned—not when play resumes and concludes. “The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension,” the statement added. “However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as ‘arbitrary’. On the contrary, the Referee’s judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.” CAS further noted that separate disciplinary sanctions had already been handed down by CAF to the FSF, head coach Pape Thiaw , and certain players over the walk-off incident. With the ruling now official, Senegal retain their second AFCON title, bringing a decisive close to one of the biggest off-pitch sagas in modern African football. *** Photo Credit: Sadio Mané/Instagram The post Senegal Reinstated as 2025 AFCON Champions After Winning CAS Appeal appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: US blacklists Megaspeed hours after Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description: Jensen Huang was barely back in charge of Nvidia when Uncle Sam slapped Megaspeed –­ the Singaporean cloud provider at the center of the scandal that cost him his job ­­– on its trade blacklist. The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has added Megaspeed and a number of affiliated businesses to its Entity List, restricting their access to American technology amid an ongoing investigation into the suspected diversion of advanced GPUs to China. The final rule [PDF], filed Monday afternoon and scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Wednesday, names seven businesses across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including Megaspeed's owner, Swiftdata, and Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix. Also in Washington's crosshairs is Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore-based subsidiary of Chinese cloud computing giant Alibaba. BIS said the businesses posed a significant risk of diverting advanced computing hardware to recipients or applications not authorized by the US government. Anyone looking to supply the seven companies with goods subject to US export controls will need a license, with applications subject to a "presumption of denial." Despite the timing of Monday's announcement, the US government's interest in Megaspeed predates the revelations about Jensen Huang's private life by some considerable margin. In a joint statement issued last week, the Departments of Justice and Commerce confirmed that the latter had opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 after spotting suspicious activity while monitoring potential violations of semiconductor export controls. Investigators requested records from Nvidia relating to both direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed in May 2025, and the GPU giant put the Singaporean outfit on its internal "no sell" list the following month. US investigators, accompanied by Singaporean law enforcement officials, subsequently visited Megaspeed's premises and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. The Justice Department has since taken the lead on the criminal investigation. Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia boss, is a businesswoman with whom Jensen was said to be having an affair – he admitted to extramarital infidelity earlier this month , although he never name-checked the Megaspeed exec. According to reports, US intelligence officials suspected she was working on behalf of Chinese intelligence, though Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations. Megaspeed maintains that its business is lawful and says Alice Huang formally left the company in August last year. It has also enlisted outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia's own Huang lasted all of 11 days in corporate exile. The chipmaker's board unanimously voted to reinstate its co-founder as president and CEO on Monday, less than a week after board chairman Harvey Jones indicated that bringing him back wasn't on the cards. The U-turn followed a lobbying campaign by some of Silicon Valley's biggest

item.content:encoded: Jensen Huang was barely back in charge of Nvidia when Uncle Sam slapped Megaspeed –­ the Singaporean cloud provider at the center of the scandal that cost him his job ­­– on its trade blacklist. The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has added Megaspeed and a number of affiliated businesses to its Entity List, restricting their access to American technology amid an ongoing investigation into the suspected diversion of advanced GPUs to China. The final rule [PDF], filed Monday afternoon and scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on Wednesday, names seven businesses across Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand, including Megaspeed's owner, Swiftdata, and Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix. Also in Washington's crosshairs is Apex Enterprise Solutions, a Singapore-based subsidiary of Chinese cloud computing giant Alibaba. BIS said the businesses posed a significant risk of diverting advanced computing hardware to recipients or applications not authorized by the US government. Anyone looking to supply the seven companies with goods subject to US export controls will need a license, with applications subject to a "presumption of denial." Despite the timing of Monday's announcement, the US government's interest in Megaspeed predates the revelations about Jensen Huang's private life by some considerable margin. In a joint statement issued last week, the Departments of Justice and Commerce confirmed that the latter had opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 after spotting suspicious activity while monitoring potential violations of semiconductor export controls. Investigators requested records from Nvidia relating to both direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed in May 2025, and the GPU giant put the Singaporean outfit on its internal "no sell" list the following month. US investigators, accompanied by Singaporean law enforcement officials, subsequently visited Megaspeed's premises and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang. The Justice Department has since taken the lead on the criminal investigation. Alice Huang, who is not related to the Nvidia boss, is a businesswoman with whom Jensen was said to be having an affair – he admitted to extramarital infidelity earlier this month , although he never name-checked the Megaspeed exec. According to reports, US intelligence officials suspected she was working on behalf of Chinese intelligence, though Beijing has rejected the espionage allegations. Megaspeed maintains that its business is lawful and says Alice Huang formally left the company in August last year. It has also enlisted outside lawyers to conduct an internal investigation. Nvidia's own Huang lasted all of 11 days in corporate exile. The chipmaker's board unanimously voted to reinstate its co-founder as president and CEO on Monday, less than a week after board chairman Harvey Jones indicated that bringing him back wasn't on the cards. The U-turn followed a lobbying campaign by some of Silicon Valley's biggest names, including Elon Musk , and some rather more consequential intervention from the White House. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he had personally persuaded Nvidia's directors to give Huang his job back. Nvidia's board said it had received assurances from senior US government officials regarding the national security implications of Huang's return. There are still plenty of people in Washington who have questions for Huang, however. The Nvidia boss is due to sit down with three congressional committees on December 1, with the chipmaker's general counsel, Tim Teter, scheduled to face lawmakers the following day. Nvidia has also established a board-level committee to oversee national security and export control compliance, putting its trade compliance personnel under the supervision of three directors. Nvidia shareholders may be delighted to have Jensen back, but the returning CEO has barely a week to prepare for his congressional grilling over the affair that helped bring about his departure. ®

item.title: YunLone Galaxy star projector review — a sub-$30 customizable night light
item.description: null The YunLone Galaxy Projector is an inexpensive but effective way to bring the marvel of space into your living room or bedroom. Costing around $28, this star projector can display beautiful dancing auroras across your walls and ceiling, and thanks to app support, a huge range of color options are available. In fact, the color combinations you can display here are almost infinite. Key specs Size: 3.54 x 3.15 x 4.72 inches (9 x 8 x 12 cm) Weight: 17.6 ounces (500 g) Bulb Type: LED Laser: Yes Operation: App and remote control Rotation: Yes Sleep timer: Yes Speaker: Yes With built-in sounds, a Bluetooth speaker and endless customization options, this really is an all-singing, all-dancing star projector. We're amazed at just how much is loaded into this package for such a low price. It's surprisingly good quality, too, with the unit itself being sturdy and made out of hard-wearing plastic. This isn't a scientific star projector, of course. For that, we'd recommend the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector . But even though the YunLone Galaxy Projector won't give you an accurate view of the Northern Hemisphere's night sky or a close-up of the moon, it's still a projector we recommend. If you're looking to create a relaxing atmosphere, it's one of the best star projectors we've reviewed. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Design The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith Solid build quality Functional rather than aesthetic design Limited buttons on the front of the unit The YunLone Galaxy Projector doesn't have the most attractive design: It's clearly built for functionality rather than aesthetics. If an aesthetically pleasing projector unit is what you're looking for, perhaps consider the Jiawen Galaxy Projector Light . You won't find nearly as many functions as the YunLone Galaxy Projector packs in, however. That isn't to say that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is ugly, though. The design is basic, with a circular shape that houses a clear globe in the middle that acts as the projector. It sits on rubberized feet, so it doesn't easily slip or move around, and it's naturally tilted, so it points slightly diagonally rather than straight up. Given the wide reach of the projector, it helps spread the aurora lights across your entire room. The projector has a solid build quality: It's plastic but feels sturdy and well-made. If you're buying for a child's bedroom, you don't need to worry about little hands being too rough when using it. Those rubber feet help prevent it from being knocked off a desk or bedside table, too. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Performance Projections produced by the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. item.dc:creator: Kim Snaith
item.content:encoded: null The YunLone Galaxy Projector is an inexpensive but effective way to bring the marvel of space into your living room or bedroom. Costing around $28, this star projector can display beautiful dancing auroras across your walls and ceiling, and thanks to app support, a huge range of color options are available. In fact, the color combinations you can display here are almost infinite. Key specs Size: 3.54 x 3.15 x 4.72 inches (9 x 8 x 12 cm) Weight: 17.6 ounces (500 g) Bulb Type: LED Laser: Yes Operation: App and remote control Rotation: Yes Sleep timer: Yes Speaker: Yes With built-in sounds, a Bluetooth speaker and endless customization options, this really is an all-singing, all-dancing star projector. We're amazed at just how much is loaded into this package for such a low price. It's surprisingly good quality, too, with the unit itself being sturdy and made out of hard-wearing plastic. This isn't a scientific star projector, of course. For that, we'd recommend the Sega Toys Homestar Classic or the Hommkiety Galaxy Projector . But even though the YunLone Galaxy Projector won't give you an accurate view of the Northern Hemisphere's night sky or a close-up of the moon, it's still a projector we recommend. If you're looking to create a relaxing atmosphere, it's one of the best star projectors we've reviewed. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Design The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith The Yunlone Galaxy Projector has a simple but effective design. Kim Snaith Solid build quality Functional rather than aesthetic design Limited buttons on the front of the unit The YunLone Galaxy Projector doesn't have the most attractive design: It's clearly built for functionality rather than aesthetics. If an aesthetically pleasing projector unit is what you're looking for, perhaps consider the Jiawen Galaxy Projector Light . You won't find nearly as many functions as the YunLone Galaxy Projector packs in, however. That isn't to say that the YunLone Galaxy Projector is ugly, though. The design is basic, with a circular shape that houses a clear globe in the middle that acts as the projector. It sits on rubberized feet, so it doesn't easily slip or move around, and it's naturally tilted, so it points slightly diagonally rather than straight up. Given the wide reach of the projector, it helps spread the aurora lights across your entire room. The projector has a solid build quality: It's plastic but feels sturdy and well-made. If you're buying for a child's bedroom, you don't need to worry about little hands being too rough when using it. Those rubber feet help prevent it from being knocked off a desk or bedside table, too. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Performance Projections produced by the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. Kim Snaith Projections produced by the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. Kim Snaith Colorful projections Great customizability via the app Wide-reaching projector As already mentioned, the YunLone Galaxy Projector isn't a scientific star projector. If you want to recreate actual constellations and close-ups of planets on your bedroom ceiling, this is not the projector for you. But if you're looking for beautiful, mesmerizing aurora-style patterns, it's a great choice. Once you're connected to the app, you can control exactly what colors the projector displays. Not only can you choose from a number of preset arrangements — labeled as seasons, colors or holidays, so you can create a mood that matches the time of year or how you feel — but you can set your own entire color scheme by choosing from a color wheel. You can also set the brightness, whether the lights will have a "breathing" effect, and how fast they ripple across your ceiling. It's a very neat touch, and it goes beyond what we'd expect to find in a star projector in this price range. If you don't want to bother with app connection, you can still set a range of colors and options from the remote control, but the options here are more limited. A projection produced by the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. (Image credit: Kim Snaith) The YunLone Galaxy Projector comes equipped with a laser, so it can project green laser stars onto your walls and ceiling. We didn't love the look of these, though, so it's good that you can turn them off independently of the aurora lights. You can also change the laser's brightness if you'd like the stars to appear dimmer. Both the laser stars and the aurora projections have a very wide reach, covering most of the walls and ceiling of the bedroom we tested the unit in. Obviously, this will vary depending on the size of your room and how far away from the ceiling/wall you place the unit, but we were pleasantly surprised by the coverage offered by this projector. YunLone Galaxy Projector: Functionality Speaker with preset sounds and Bluetooth Remote control App functionality The YunLone Galaxy Projector has a companion app that can be downloaded onto an Android or Apple smartphone. Once the app is set up and paired with your unit, you have full control over the colors, speed and brightness of your projections. The pairing process isn't entirely straightforward, however, with no simple way of forcing the projector to enter pairing mode. The instructions tell you to quickly turn the unit on and off three times, but it took several attempts before we successfully put the projector into pairing mode. The YunLone Galaxy Projector's on-body buttons and remote control. Kim Snaith Thankfully, once that's done, it should stay paired with your smartphone permanently so you won't have to repeat the process. And the app itself is very easy to use, working seamlessly to change the colors of the projection unit. The bundled remote control (which requires two AAA batteries, not included) is a little more complex than most, offering a range of buttons to control both the built-in speaker and the light itself. We'd highly recommend opting for the app option as it gives you much better control over the unit, but if your smartphone is unavailable, you can at least set basic color and speed with the remote. You can connect a music player to the projector via Bluetooth to play your own audio through its built-in speaker. The quality is decent rather than outstanding: It obviously doesn't match the sound of a specialist speaker, but it's as good as we'd expect any $28 speaker to be. It lacks the bass that music requires to sound "complete" but will be ideal for listening to audiobooks and podcasts. In a neat touch, the YunLone Galaxy Projector also has eight built-in sound effects, including white noise, waves, lullabies and a storm, which some users may find relaxing and good to fall asleep to. The remote control unit for the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. Kim snaith The app of the Yunlone Galaxy Projector. Kim Snaith Should I buy the YunLone Galaxy Projector? We have been thoroughly impressed with what the YunLone Galaxy Projector offers. Its projections are beautiful auroras that dance across your ceiling, and the ability to fully customize the color and speed is something that we really didn't expect to find at a $28 price point. If you're on a budget and looking for a non-scientific projector to use to relax and unwind with, we really don't think you can find a better unit. If, however, you want something that offers more scientific projections, you'll need to look elsewhere. Sega Toys' range of projectors, including the Homestar Flux and the Homestar Classic , is excellent but comes with a much bigger price tag. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector is worth considering too, offering realistic projections but with a price tag closer to $50. The good thing about these projectors is that they come with interchangeable discs, able to display various images of space. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector has several discs in the box, but you'll need to buy extra discs for the Sega Toys range, so that’s an extra cost to factor in.

item.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
item.description: null (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system. Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. Why is it incredible? For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth. But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid , meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet. Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

item.title: Chinese media hail Huang’s Nvidia return with warning over ‘witch-hunts’
item.description: State-run Global Times says reports about CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy were ‘malicious’ Trump made up to $15m on Nvidia stock after Huang’s return Nvidia staff: what do you think of Jensen Huang’s return as chief executive? Chinese media have reacted with glee to the dramatic reinstatement of Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia, with one commentary warning against future “witch-hunts”. An article published on Tuesday in the state-run outlet the Global Times said US media reports about Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset were “malicious” and “negatively impacted American public perception of China”. Continue reading...

item.title: Olam Agri Rewards Loyal Dealers at Customer Awards & Recognition Night
item.description: Olam Agri ’s wheat milling and pasta business, Crown Flour Mill ( CFM ) Limited, honoured its top customers, dealers and distributors at its Customer Awards & Recognition Night, marking more than 15 years of partnership. Held under the theme “Celebrating Partnerships, Rewarding Excellence,” the event brought together company leadership and long-standing partners from Northern, Eastern and Western Nigeria. It paid tribute to the distributors who built markets and the dealers who remained committed through shifting economic conditions. Their enterprise and confidence have carried CFM’s products to customers and communities across the country. The highlight of the evening was the rewarding of CFM’s best-performing dealers across three categories: Trailblazer, Sterling and Titan. Winners received 5-tonne, 10-tonne and 15-tonne trucks, as well as baking ovens. The night closed with the presentation of a 45-tonne truck to the overall best-performing dealer. L-R: Charles Babarimisa, Head of Sales; Siddharth Suri, Vice President/Business Head; Nitin Mehta, Managing Director, all of Crown Flour Mill (CFM) Limited; and Alhaji Oluwasesan Sose, the overall best-performing distributor and winner of a 45-tonne truck, during the presentation of award prizes. Nitin Mehta, Business Head, Wheat Milling & Pasta Business, Olam Agri, said the milestone reflects far more than time. “Fifteen years of growing together represents relationships built on trust, shared ambition and resilience. Our dealers and distributors have helped us extend our market reach, serve customers better and strengthen our position in the industry. Through changing market dynamics and different challenges, the strength of our partnerships has been a constant source of resilience.” Sanusi Modinat (5th from right), a dealer, with her award and the key to a 15-tonne truck, her reward for her performance. Bolaji Anifowose , Vice President & Commercial, Olam Agri, described dealers as strategic partners rather than an extension of the distribution network. “Their market knowledge, entrepreneurial drive and commitment connect our brands to consumers across the country. Our focus now is on strengthening these partnerships, improving market reach, enhancing distribution efficiency and creating more opportunities for our partners to grow. A stronger dealer network means a stronger business.” The overall best-performing dealer, Alhaji Oluwaseun Sose, called the award a proud moment. “My relationship with the company has been built on trust, consistency and a shared commitment to growth. It has been a journey of learning, overcoming challenges and identifying opportunities together. This recognition encourages me to keep striving for excellence.” The runner-up, Opeyemi Sanusi Modinat, praised the company’s collaborative approach. “Our partnership has given us opportunities to grow, expand our market presence and serve more customers. What makes it special is the understanding that our success matters too.

item.title: Claude Ship puts AI at the helm of pull request approvals
item.description: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship to review, fix, and approve pull requests (PRs), offering more AI automation to help teams handle the output of AI coding tools. Claude Ship combines the generally available Code Review service with two new agents in beta: PR Steward and Claude Approvals. It is available to Claude Team and Enterprise customers using GitHub repositories. Anthropic said : "On the Claude Code team, Claude writes most of our code, and we wanted everything after the PR to move that fast too." Its stated goal is to "ship code as fast as teams write it." One consequence of the AI coding revolution is the sheer amount of agent output, which requires review and approval before going live. Claude Ship is one way to address that by automating more of the workflow. PR Steward works through failing continuous integration (CI) checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback. Claude Approvals can actually approve a PR, something that might rattle the nerves of some engineers. Claude Approvals applies an approval policy, written by the team as a file in the repository. "Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios," Anthropic said. The company advised caution: "For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light." While developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests (depending on their permissions and the repository's branch rules) with a /ship command in Claude Code, administrators can set up the rules on a repository-by-repository basis. "Claude Approvals starts when a connected repository has a policy file on its default branch, and an admin can turn it off," Anthropic said. "Teams set the pace. They can start with one repository, choose a review level and when reviews run, set a monthly spend limit, and run their approval policy in observe mode until they trust it." The extra automation also brings extra charges. Usage is token-based, and even observe-only approval policies can incur costs if they invoke classifiers or Code Review. Anthropic also includes the familiar disclaimer: "Claude Ship uses AI and may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities, or other issues." The Register spoke to an engineer who works for a company that uses Claude. They were a little cynical about the whole thing, saying: "It just seems like a glorification of what I already use Claude on – git merge or git rebase. "Our golden rule so far with Git is to limit Claude to read operations there; this layer of separation still lets devs stay in control and allows them a judgment of the AI changes – what to keep, tweak, or commit. "If that's offloaded to Claude and it has Git history-rewrite access, the devs will lose that overview and judgment opportunity." item.content:encoded: Anthropic has introduced Claude Ship to review, fix, and approve pull requests (PRs), offering more AI automation to help teams handle the output of AI coding tools. It is available to Claude Team and Enterprise customers using GitHub repositories. One consequence of the AI coding revolution is the sheer amount of agent output, which requires review and approval before going live. Claude Ship is one way to address that by automating more of the workflow. PR Steward works through failing continuous integration (CI) checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback. Claude Approvals can actually approve a PR, something that might rattle the nerves of some engineers. Claude Approvals applies an approval policy, written by the team as a file in the repository. "Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios," Anthropic said. The company advised caution: "For most customers, we recommend enabling this first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals' green light." While developers can try Claude Ship on their own pull requests (depending on their permissions and the repository's branch rules) with a /ship command in Claude Code, administrators can set up the rules on a repository-by-repository basis. "Claude Approvals starts when a connected repository has a policy file on its default branch, and an admin can turn it off," Anthropic said. "Teams set the pace. They can start with one repository, choose a review level and when reviews run, set a monthly spend limit, and run their approval policy in observe mode until they trust it." The extra automation also brings extra charges. Usage is token-based, and even observe-only approval policies can incur costs if they invoke classifiers or Code Review. Anthropic also includes the familiar disclaimer: "Claude Ship uses AI and may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities, or other issues." The Register spoke to an engineer who works for a company that uses Claude. They were a little cynical about the whole thing, saying: "It just seems like a glorification of what I already use Claude on – git merge or git rebase. "Our golden rule so far with Git is to limit Claude to read operations there; this layer of separation still lets devs stay in control and allows them a judgment of the AI changes – what to keep, tweak, or commit. "If that's offloaded to Claude and it has Git history-rewrite access, the devs will lose that overview and judgment opportunity." How much authority Claude receives depends on the organization's configuration. Approval is not the same as merging, and existing branch protections and required checks still apply. Anthropic's answer to a growing queue of AI-generated changes is more AI. Teams still have to decide which decisions they're prepared to delegate. ®

item.title: Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk
item.description: Mentors, mentees, professionals and members of the public gathered at Eko Atlantic, Lagos, on Saturday, November 14, 2026, for the annual Women in Successful Careers (WISCAR) Mentoring Walk . Led by WISCAR Founder and Chairperson, Amina Oyagbola , the walk forms part of the lead-up to the organisation’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference. Participants were paired up for the walk along the Eko Atlantic, each with someone they had not met before. At the end of the route, they switched to new mentor-mentee partners for a short mentoring session, which gave everyone two fresh conversations in one morning. Back at the meeting point, participants shared what they had learnt from their partners, from career advice to personal lessons. Nutritionist Sherese Ijewere then led a session on healthy eating and answered questions on everyday food choices. Coach Bobbie Tee of Happy Heart Fitness, closed the morning with a Zumba session. Next stop: the conference The walk sets the stage for WISCAR’s 18th Annual Leadership and Mentoring Conference , themed “ Courage in Action: Shaping Policies and Structures for Inclusive Progress. ” The conference takes place on Saturday, November 28, 2026, at the Civic Centre, Lagos. Highlights include: A keynote from Dr Ndidi Nwuneli , former President and CEO of the ONE Campaign and Founder of LEAP Africa, who will also receive this year’s Distinguished WISCAR Award. Speakers including Badejo-Okusanya , SAN, President of the Nigerian Bar Association, and Mallam Ahmed Ladan Gobir, President of the Chartered Institute of Personnel Management (CIPM) The launch of WISCAR’s CIPM-endorsed Corporate Mentoring Playbook The graduation of Cohort 2 of the Women in Law Mentoring Programme Register now at https://wiscar.ng/almc . Sponsored Content The post Inside the 2026 WISCAR Mentoring Walk appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: The Nvidia case is just the latest episode of Trump disregarding intelligence
item.description: Trump’s reaction to sensitive information that contradicts his worldview mirrors his conduct towards war with Iran Donald Trump’s unwillingness to heed warnings of suspected Chinese penetration of the tech giant Nvidia follows a pattern of the US president ignoring sensitive intelligence that contradicts his world view. Trump disregarded repeated information that the company’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, was having an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy that threatened to undermine Washington’s geostrategically vital goal of pipping China for global supremacy in the artificial intelligence race. Continue reading...

item.title: China launches Pakistani astronaut to Tiangong space station, its 1st international visitor, alongside Shenzhou-24 crew (video)
item.description: null China launched an international astronaut, Pakistan's first space traveler to reach orbit, to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, marking a significant milestone for international participation in the Chinese space program. A Long March 2F rocket lifted off with the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 is China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong space station , a three-module orbital lab that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022. Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight makes history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023 .) The Chinese Manned Space Engineering (Image credit: VCG/VCG via Getty Images) China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025 , with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training. We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch. This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest. The six astronauts of China's Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 crews give thumb's up signs in blue jumpsuits on the Tiangong Space Station. (Image credit: CMSE) Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu. Pakistan's first orbital astronaut, pilot Mohammed Zishan Ali (left), salutes alongside Shenzhou-24 crewmates Tang Hongbo (center) and Wu Yi before their launch into orbit. (Image credit: Xu Xun/VCG via Getty Images) Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. Pakistan's first orbital astronaut, pilot Mohammed Zishan Ali (left), salutes alongside Shenzhou-24 crewmates Tang Hongbo (center) and Wu Yi before their launch into orbit. (Image credit: Xu Xun/VCG via Getty Images) Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24 . Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

item.title: FCC proposes 'tit-for-tat' restrictions on foreign satellite operators
item.description: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will vote in December on proposals [PDF] that would restrict foreign satellite operators in the same way their home countries restrict US providers. The telecoms regulator says the move is to "ensure reciprocity and fair dealing" in the rules governing satellite operators. The main aim appears to be hitting back at European efforts to build up the region's own space communications industries. According to the FCC, the US has so far welcomed satellite systems licensed abroad on a level playing field, but that regulators elsewhere have begun holding US systems to different rules than they apply to their own domestic suppliers. "This has operated to the disadvantage of American satellite providers that are or may be burdened with regulatory and spectrum limitations that their competitors in foreign nations simply do not face," said FCC chairman Brendan Carr. The FCC has singled out the EU's Digital Networks Act , which proposes harmonized connectivity rules across the bloc. A separate proposal would overhaul authorization for mobile satellite services (MSS) in the 2 GHz band after existing rights expire in May 2027. Earlier this year, the FCC laid out some of its concerns, saying that EU-wide authorization of satellite spectrum would replace the national licensing by member states "with which US satellite operators have become accustomed," and could require wholesale relicensing of any US systems operating in Europe. "The FCC voting on foreign satellite companies is consistent with the Digital Networks Act, but is more of a response to the EU's decisions on how it plans to allocate the EU-wide 2 GHz spectrum," CCS Insight analyst Joe Gardiner told The Register . "The EU outlined in its proposal that, for two-thirds of the spectrum, only operators based in the EU with EU ownership and aligned with the EU's strategic goals will be considered for the spectrum. "This has locked out companies like SpaceX and Amazon Leo from attaining access to spectrum that is highly valuable for satellite direct-to-device services. The US government is looking to retaliate, to support the US constellations that would have attempted to win this EU-wide spectrum." Following an initial consultation in March, the FCC will vote in December on opening a rulemaking to reconsider how foreign-licensed satellite operators gain access to the US market. "It is time for this regulatory asymmetry to end," Carr said, adding that the FCC now proposes to mirror any regulations that foreign nations apply to American satellite providers. "If there are limits or restrictions on American providers operating abroad, then the notice proposes to apply those or similar regulatory restraints to satellite providers from those countries that are operating here." item.dc:creator: Dan Robinson
item.content:encoded: The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) will vote in December on proposals [PDF] that would restrict foreign satellite operators in the same way their home countries restrict US providers. The telecoms regulator says the move is to "ensure reciprocity and fair dealing" in the rules governing satellite operators. The main aim appears to be hitting back at European efforts to build up the region's own space communications industries. According to the FCC, the US has so far welcomed satellite systems licensed abroad on a level playing field, but that regulators elsewhere have begun holding US systems to different rules than they apply to their own domestic suppliers. "This has operated to the disadvantage of American satellite providers that are or may be burdened with regulatory and spectrum limitations that their competitors in foreign nations simply do not face," said FCC chairman Brendan Carr. The FCC has singled out the EU's Digital Networks Act , which proposes harmonized connectivity rules across the bloc. A separate proposal would overhaul authorization for mobile satellite services (MSS) in the 2 GHz band after existing rights expire in May 2027. Earlier this year, the FCC laid out some of its concerns, saying that EU-wide authorization of satellite spectrum would replace the national licensing by member states "with which US satellite operators have become accustomed," and could require wholesale relicensing of any US systems operating in Europe. "The FCC voting on foreign satellite companies is consistent with the Digital Networks Act, but is more of a response to the EU's decisions on how it plans to allocate the EU-wide 2 GHz spectrum," CCS Insight analyst Joe Gardiner told The Register . "The EU outlined in its proposal that, for two-thirds of the spectrum, only operators based in the EU with EU ownership and aligned with the EU's strategic goals will be considered for the spectrum. "This has locked out companies like SpaceX and Amazon Leo from attaining access to spectrum that is highly valuable for satellite direct-to-device services. The US government is looking to retaliate, to support the US constellations that would have attempted to win this EU-wide spectrum." Following an initial consultation in March, the FCC will vote in December on opening a rulemaking to reconsider how foreign-licensed satellite operators gain access to the US market. "It is time for this regulatory asymmetry to end," Carr said, adding that the FCC now proposes to mirror any regulations that foreign nations apply to American satellite providers. "If there are limits or restrictions on American providers operating abroad, then the notice proposes to apply those or similar regulatory restraints to satellite providers from those countries that are operating here." Britain is outside the EU, but does not escape the FCC's ire. The agency previously claimed the UK Space Agency allocates a significant portion of its budget, circa 75 percent in 2023/24, to European Space Agency (ESA) procurements, which US companies are not allowed to bid for as America is not a member of ESA. British satellite operators could therefore face restrictions on access to the US market if the FCC adopts reciprocal measures. The UK's space industry generated £18.6 billion in income in 2022/23, according to the UK Space Agency. ®

item.title: Russia launches Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station (video)
item.description: null Russia's latest freighter is on its way to the International Space Station. The robotic Progress 97 cargo craft launched atop a Soyuz rocket from the Russia-run Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan today (Nov. 24) at 5:17 a.m. EST (1013 GMT; 3:17 p.m. Baikonur time), carrying several tons of supplies for the astronauts aboard the orbiting lab. If all goes to plan, Progress 97 will arrive at the International Space Station (ISS) on Thursday (Nov. 26), docking with its Poisk module. But the freighter won't stay at that particular locale for long. A Russian Soyuz rocket launches the uncrewed Progress 97 cargo ship to the International Space Station from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan on Nov. 24, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The cosmonauts currently living on the ISS — Pyotr Dubrov, Anna Kikina and Sergey Teteryatnikov — will unload Progress 97 through Poisk. But the freighter will then hop over to a different port, according to journalist and space historian Anatoly Zak: the aft one of the PrK transfer tunnel, which leads to Russia's Zvezda service module. The PrK port is the best site for engine burns that boost the orbit of the ISS, a service that Progress freighters regularly provide. But Progress 97 cannot unload its cargo through that port because the PrK transfer tunnel has been sealed off, due to an ongoing air leak that was first documented in 2019. Progress-97 is therefore "the first cargo mission scheduled to unload its cargo and perform orbit corrections of the ISS at different docking ports," Zak wrote on the site he runs, RussianSpaceWeb.com. Progress 96 cargo spacecraft packed with science and supplies approaches the International Space Station for a docking on Sept. 19, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The Progress 97 mission, which Russia calls Progress MS-36, was originally expected to launch this past August, according to Zak. But the liftoff was pushed back several times, most significantly by the collapse of the service platform at Baikonur's Site 31 in November 2025. It took Russia about three months to repair the platform, leading to a series of delays. Progress 97 will likely stay docked to the ISS for about six months, after which it will be loaded up with trash and sent home to burn up in Earth's atmosphere . Japan's HTV-X vehicle and Northrop Grumman's Cygnus spacecraft are similarly expendable. The only currently operational ISS cargo craft that's reusable is SpaceX's Dragon capsule, which makes parachute-aided ocean splashdowns at the end of its missions.

item.title: 9/UX brings a classic Mac feel to 9front
item.description: Bringing a classic MacOS Finder to Linux is all very well, but there's no shortage of Linux desktops… however, bringing one to 9front is even more unexpected – and even more useful. 9/UX is a new project by Jeff " Progrium " Lindsay, who was one of the people behind Docker, Webhooks, and more. When you follow that link, and you should, pay close attention to what looks like a screenshot at the top. It is not an image. It's a real live executing instance of the OS, running inside your web browser, running on top of hyper9 . (That is worth reading too – it's an impressive project in its own right.) As its GitHub repository describes, 9/UX is a "Macintosh-inspired graphical environment for 9front." The README provides more detail: "9/UX brings the classic Mac and A/UX desktop experience (a spatial desktop, a global menu bar, consistent controls and dialogs, icons, and resource-driven presentation) to 9front, built the Plan 9 way: rio and libdraw draw the screen, 9P exposes every application's UI state and commands as files, namespaces define the working environment, the plumber opens documents, and ndb holds human-editable metadata." Lindsay introduced 9/UX earlier this month in a short X thread , saying he "made my own kind of A/UX but on Plan 9." In its creator's own words, "it's slop", but this is kind of interesting, original, creative bot-assisted coding that we enjoy looking at. At the end of last week, he returned to explain more : "9/UX isn’t just a pretty Mac-style UI on Plan 9. It's filesystem inspectable. Shell scriptable. Even the Mac resource file format can be used through the filesystem." Regular readers may have noticed that The Reg FOSS desk is fascinated by Plan 9 and its FOSS continuation 9front. We've written and presented at length about this remarkable OS, and tried to explain its FOSS continuation 9front several times . But even with the best will we can muster, its unique GUI is not an especially friendly or easy one. Its idiosyncratic UI was inspired by the late great Niklaus Wirth 's unbelievably tiny Oberon OS, which we have written about before . It's cryptic, and that's being generous. The research and development effort that led to Unix didn't stop when Unix 7th Edition escaped from the Bell Labs in 1981 and mutated into Unix System III. The industry enthusiastically adopted System III and later System V. A decade after 7th Edition Unix, Linux became a GPL version of something very like that traditional Unix, closely followed by the BSDs – and between them, they have very effectively distracted most of the FOSS world ever since. Even so, Research Unix lived on, saw 8th, 9th, and 10th editions, and then was replaced by Plan 9. In 1996, many of Plan 9's limitations were overcome by Inferno – whose revival as InferNode we covered this week. We always vaguely thought that if 9front were to receive an improved GUI that was slightly more compliant with later GUI design standards, it might be with a version of the Inferno UI …

A new, easier, and yet still simple, clean and attractive desktop for 9front is here, and it looks like classic MacOS from the era of Apple's 68030 Unix A/UX. We do not think the chances are high that the 9front community will adopt this with enthusiasm. Even so, there is an AI programming manual for agents , and we've seen some interesting looking LLM-assisted 9front apps of late. Several can be found in the agent9 distributio n , which includes LLM-assisted ports of C++ , Python , and Rust , plus a version of DOSbox , and even a package manager called pac9 .®

item.title: GTA VI’s jaw-dropping success: in figures
item.description: Content creators have produced hundreds of millions of hours of video game since its launch Grand Theft Auto ( GTA) VI became the largest video game release of all time last week and while it is hard to say exactly how many people are playing the game (current estimates say at least 30 million), there are plenty of other jaw-dropping data points we do know. Data on streaming the game suggests that only two days into its release a cumulative 364.5m hours have been watched – roughly 41,000 years of content. Put another way, that translates to more than 41,000 years worth of people riffling through cash registers, hanging drywall, birding, diving or hijacking jets. That’s according to streaming data from Streams Charts, a data and analytics company that has been tracking Rockstar Game’s long-awaited title. Continue reading...

item.title: Watch November's full Beaver Moon live online today with supermoon livestream
item.description: null Editor's Note: The November full supermoon dazzled stargazers with a spectacular show overnight on Nov. 24. Check out our photo wrap article to see spectacular images of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world. November's full moon rises tonight (Nov. 24)! You can see live telescopic views of the "Beaver supermoon" courtesy of the Virtual Telescope Project (VTP). The free YouTube livestream begins at 10:30 a.m. EST (1530 GMT) and will feature live views of the moon captured by a suite of robotic telescopes in Manciano, Italy, weather permitting. Today's stream features expert commentary from VTP founder Gianluca Masi, along with photos of previous full moons shining above historic landmarks in the heart of Rome. What makes the November full moon special? November's full moon is often called the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the industrious animals are hard at work building dams and preparing for the winter months, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . It is also set to be a spectacular supermoon , which reaches peak illumination while within 90% of perigee — the closest point to Earth in the moon's 27-day elliptical orbit. You might like: November full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Beaver Moon . Supermoons can be up to 13% larger and 30% brighter than the smallest full moon of the year, which occurred in May earlier this year as the natural satellite shone opposite the sun in Earth's sky while close to apogee, when it is farthest from our planet. Interested in capturing your own mesmerizing views of the full moon? Then be sure to read our guide to photographing the lunar disk , along with our roundups of the best cameras and lenses for astrophotography . Editor's Note: If you would like to share your photos of the Beaver Moon with Space.com's readers, then please send your photo(s), along with your name, location and thoughts to spacephotos@space.com.

item.title: Nigeria and Tanzania to Co-Host Inaugural WHAS in Abuja, Mobilising Continental Action for Better Women’s Health
item.description: The Governments of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the United Republic of Tanzania will jointly host the inaugural Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS) 2026 on Tuesday, 1 December 2026, at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja, from 12:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Held under the theme “Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health,” WHAS 2026 will convene approximately 300 senior decision-makers, including Heads of State, First Ladies, Ministers of Health and Finance, African Union (AU) leadership, development finance institutions, philanthropists, and health innovators, to move Africa from political commitment to accountable investment and delivery. As a Nigeria-led, African-owned continental platform, WHAS is designed to advance women’s health across the entire life course, encompassing maternal, reproductive, and gynaecological health, noncommunicable diseases, and menopause, by treating women’s health not merely as a social priority, but as a central driver of Africa’s economic and social progress. Investing in women’s health is also an investment in Africa’s productivity, economic resilience, and future prosperity. WHAS 2026 bridges the flagship African Union Champion mandates of the two co-hosting nations. Serving as founding convener, Nigeria brings the political leadership and health workforce agenda championed by His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, AU Champion for Human Resources for Health and Community Health Delivery Partnership. Nationally, WHAS is anchored in the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, CON , with presidential facilitation by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Women’s Health (OSSAP-WH) . As co-host, Tanzania brings its continental leadership on maternal and child health, championed by Her Excellency, President Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, AU Champion for Maternal and Child Health, advancing the Continental Roadmap on Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) 2026–2030 and its Three Zeros: Zero Home Delivery, Zero Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths, and Zero Unvaccinated Children. Tanzania’s co-hosting is delivered through the Ministry of Health, led by Hon. Mohamed Omary Mchengerwa , Minister of Health, and the Secretariat of the African Union Champion for Maternal and Child Health. item.content:encoded: The Governments of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the United Republic of Tanzania will jointly host the inaugural Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS) 2026 on Tuesday, 1 December 2026, at the State House Banquet Hall, Abuja, from 12:00 PM to 7:00 PM. Held under the theme “Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health,” WHAS 2026 will convene approximately 300 senior decision-makers, including Heads of State, First Ladies, Ministers of Health and Finance, African Union (AU) leadership, development finance institutions, philanthropists, and health innovators, to move Africa from political commitment to accountable investment and delivery. As a Nigeria-led, African-owned continental platform, WHAS is designed to advance women’s health across the entire life course, encompassing maternal, reproductive, and gynaecological health, noncommunicable diseases, and menopause, by treating women’s health not merely as a social priority, but as a central driver of Africa’s economic and social progress. Investing in women’s health is also an investment in Africa’s productivity, economic resilience, and future prosperity. WHAS 2026 bridges the flagship African Union Champion mandates of the two co-hosting nations. Serving as founding convener, Nigeria brings the political leadership and health workforce agenda championed by His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, AU Champion for Human Resources for Health and Community Health Delivery Partnership. Nationally, WHAS is anchored in the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare under the leadership of the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, CON , with presidential facilitation by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Women’s Health (OSSAP-WH) . As co-host, Tanzania brings its continental leadership on maternal and child health, championed by Her Excellency, President Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, AU Champion for Maternal and Child Health, advancing the Continental Roadmap on Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCAH) 2026–2030 and its Three Zeros: Zero Home Delivery, Zero Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths, and Zero Unvaccinated Children. Tanzania’s co-hosting is delivered through the Ministry of Health, led by Hon. Mohamed Omary Mchengerwa , Minister of Health, and the Secretariat of the African Union Champion for Maternal and Child Health. Speaking ahead of WHAS 2026, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, CON , Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, described the Summit as an important platform for advancing collaboration, shared learning, and African ownership of the women’s health agenda: “ The Women’s Health Africa Summit is a great platform for bringing together leaders, advocates, practitioners, academics and financiers to identify gaps, mobilise action and facilitate shared learning across countries. Indeed, women’s health is a global issue, and even wealthier countries continue to face significant gaps in this area. Ultimately, responsibility lies with us as leaders on the continent. We must take ownership of our health priorities.” Echoing the commitment to continental solidarity and measurable progress, Hon. Ummy Ally Mwalimu , Special Adviser to the President of the United Republic of Tanzania on Maternal and Child Health and Head of the Secretariat of the African Union Champion for Maternal and Child Health, highlighted the synergy between both nations’ leadership agendas: “Under the leadership of Her Excellency President Dr. Samia Suluhu Hassan, AU Champion for Maternal and Child Health, Tanzania is proud to co-host WHAS with Nigeria. Collaboration between our two AU Champions is an implementation imperative, not simply a matter of institutional goodwill. Coordinated leadership is essential to align workforce investment, community health delivery, sustainable financing and accountability with country-led priorities, avoid fragmented efforts and translate continental commitments into measurable results. The Three Zeros of the Continental RMNCAH Roadmap depend on competent, adequately supported frontline health workers, functional referral systems and effective community outreach. WHAS, under the theme ‘Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health’, provides a timely platform for these shared commitments.” Pathfinder International , serving as Lead Technical Partner, is supporting programme design, technical content, strategic partnerships, and efforts to connect political leadership, financing, and country-led implementation, including practical follow-up beyond the Summit. Highlighting the broader vision of WHAS, Dr. Adanna Steinacker , Senior Special Assistant to the President on Women’s Health, noted: “ For too long, women’s health has been treated as a secondary concern or viewed narrowly through a single stage of life. WHAS changes that paradigm, bringing African governments, capital, and innovators together to back women’s health across the entire life course as a core pillar of our continent’s social and economic future.” Structured around three enduring pillars: Innovation, Financing, and Delivery , WHAS 2026 will focus on strengthening the frontline and specialist health workforce required to deliver quality care to women and girls at every stage of life. WHAS will seek to secure an initial set of country and institutional commitments, including accelerated action on neglected gynaecological conditions, while establishing an enduring framework for African-led collaboration and post-summit accountability. Event : Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS) 2026 Date : Tuesday, 1 December 2026 Time : 12:00 PM – 7:00 PM WAT Venue : State House Banquet Hall, Abuja, Nigeria Theme : Health Workforce for Better Women’s Health Co-Hosts : Federal Republic of Nigeria and United Republic of Tanzania Lead Technical Partner : Pathfinder International Related milestones : Joint Roadmap Dialogue, Addis Ababa, 24 November 2026; Political and Delivery Dialogue at WHAS, Abuja, 1 December 2026 For more information and partnerships, visit womenshealthafricasummit.com . About the Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS) The Women’s Health Africa Summit (WHAS) is a Nigeria-led, African-owned continental platform dedicated to advancing women’s health across the life course. Built on the three pillars of Innovation, Financing, and Delivery, WHAS brings together governments, political leaders, financing institutions, innovators, and delivery partners to strengthen health systems, mobilise domestic and international capital, and accelerate equitable access to quality healthcare for women across Africa. item.title: CrowdStrike splashes $44B on Zscaler, customers brace for the bill
item.description: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in what would be the biggest cybersecurity acquisition on record, and customers are already bracing for pricier renewals. The all-stock deal, announced on Monday , will see Zscaler shareholders receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares for every share they own, representing a 34 percent premium on Friday's closing price. The transaction dwarfs even Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security upstart Wiz . Buying Zscaler gives CrowdStrike a sizeable foothold in the network security market, where it will be going up against the likes of Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet. The plan is to combine Falcon's endpoint protection capabilities with Zscaler's zero-trust network security technology, giving customers a single platform for securing devices and the connections between them. Naturally, there's an AI angle to the biggest cyber deal in history. CrowdStrike reckons owning both technologies will allow it to keep tabs on what AI agents are doing on corporate devices, where they're connecting, and what data they're getting their hands on. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz described the proposed combination as "cybersecurity’s operating system." The acquisition also gives CrowdStrike's salespeople plenty to get excited about. Around 8,000 Zscaler customers don't currently buy CrowdStrike's wares, and the companies already have more than 2,000 customers in common. CrowdStrike reckons it can boost its annualized revenue by around $1 billion within 30 months of closing the deal by selling more products to the two companies' existing customers. Some of those customers, however, don't sound particularly keen on being cross-sold to. "As a zscaler customer, this does worry me. Cost increase, forced move to Falcon, integration issues, etc," wrote one sysadmin. Another, whose organization already uses both vendors' products, added: "I think they're both great products but I imagine they'll jack up the price for our next renewal. Fun."
